memo: # AskBack AI 老師 — 技術決策備忘錄（2026-10-14） > 範圍：本地 voice-clone TTS 選型、3090 前處理流程、Remotion 資料驅動渲染器、風險清單、SKILL.md 修改。所有事實皆附來源；無法從一手來源確認者標 **UNVERIFIED**。 --- ## 1. 本地 voice-clone TTS 的選擇 ### 結論先講 截至 2026-10-14，**沒有任何一個開放模型被證實在「臺灣國語 + 繁體 + 多音字控制」這條軸上優於 BreezyVoice**。新模型（CosyVoice3、Qwen3-TTS、GLM-TTS、VoxCPM2、IndexTTS）的 CER/SIM 優勢全部來自 Seed-TTS test-zh（簡體、中國大陸語者）的自評數字，沒有任何 zh-TW 評測，也找不到任何「複製臺灣語者」的第一手回報（TTS 研究報告 notes；zh-TW 報告 (b)）。因此採 **「首選維持 BreezyVoice、備援引入 Fun-CosyVoice3、以 A/B 評測決定是否切換」** 的策略，而不是直接換引擎。 ### 首選：BreezyVoice-300M（MediaTek Research）— 維持現狀，但補強 - **理由**：唯一明確針對臺灣國語訓練的開放 TTS；原生吃繁體；行內注音覆寫 `今天天氣真好[:ㄏㄠ3]`；內建 G2PW 自動標注多音字（<500 頻字 / 讀音異於常見讀音者）；論文 TCMD PER 0.80%、SSL-MOS 4.46、SIM 92.29%（https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice ；https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17790 ；https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/main/single_inference.py）。 - **License**：Apache-2.0（GitHub + HF）。範例音檔 tc_speaker.wav 商用疑問 #15 無人回覆 → 只用自己的參考音檔（https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/issues/15）。 - **VRAM**：官方未列；CosyVoice-1 等級模型，估 <6 GB（UNVERIFIED）。issue #10 顯示 CPU 結果劣於 GPU → 一律在 3090 上跑（https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/issues/10）。 - **安裝 pins（HEAD 仍是 d592c9d，2025-06-21，16 個月無程式碼變更，故姊妹專案的 pin 依然有效）**：Python 3.10；`torch==2.3.1 torchaudio==2.3.1`（cu118 index）；`onnxruntime-gpu==1.16.0`；`openai-whisper==20231117`；`WeTextProcessing==1.0.3`；`deepspeed==0.14.2`；`diffusers==0.32.0`；g2pw、opencc-python-reimplemented 未釘版；ttsfrd 0.3.9 cp310 wheel；需 `PYTHONUTF8=1`（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/main/requirements.txt ；https://api.github.com/repos/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/commits?per_page=5）。 - **繁體與多音字**：繁體直接輸入；多音字由 G2PW 自動標 + 每課 override 表手動補 `字[:ㄓㄨㄥ4]`（長/行/樂/重/和/數）。注意：繼承的 WeTextProcessing 1.0.3 `Normalizer` master 預設 `traditional_to_simple=True`，BreezyVoice 是否整句轉簡 **UNVERIFIED**（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenet-e2e/WeTextProcessing/master/tn/chinese/normalizer.py）。數字與算式（「1598-260」）一律在送進任何引擎前自行以繁體 verbalize。 - **參考音檔**：16 kHz mono（`load_wav(path,16000)`），繼承 CosyVoice ≤30 s assert（對此 fork UNVERIFIED），建議 6–15 s、乾淨單人、無 BGM；一定要給 transcript，不要讓它用 whisper-base 自動轉（zh-TW 很弱）。 - **缺點（為何還要備援）**：2025-06 起停更；CosyVoice-1 架構，相似度理論上低於 CosyVoice2/3 血統（推論，UNVERIFIED）；無 CER/SIM 公開數字；無 speaker cache（#8/#12）；torch 2.3.1 cu118 舊 stack。MediaTek 2026 的「BreezyVoice 26」是台語 TTS、權重未釋出，官方部落格明說無國語 TTS 更新（https://www.mediatek.com/zh-tw/tek-talk-blogs/mediatek-research-breeze-3 ；https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/issues/14 ；https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19259）。 ### 備援（A/B 候選）：Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 + `llm.rl.pt` - **正確識別碼**：HF 只有 `FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512` 一個 repo；「_RL」不是獨立模型，RL 權重是同 repo 內的 `llm.rl.pt`，載入需把它改名/symlink 成 `llm.pt`（維護者 #1780）（https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512/tree/main ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1780）。GitHub 已 301 到 QwenAudio/CosyVoice。 - **理由**：Apache-2.0（程式與權重）；test-zh CER 1.21→0.81（RL），但 SIM 78.0→77.4 略降；拼音 inpainting 可覆寫多音字；社群在 3090 實測 ~5.2 GB VRAM（二手，fengin）；fp32 eager 每句 ~4–8 s（推估自 3090 Ti 數據，UNVERIFIED）（https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice ；https://github.com/fengin/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512-Deploy ；https://github.com/instavar/cosyvoice3-lora-finetuning）。 - **安裝 pins（與 BreezyVoice 不能共用 venv：cu121 vs cu118）**：Python 3.10；`torch==2.3.1 torchaudio==2.3.1`（`--extra-index-url .../cu121`）；**`transformers==4.51.3` 硬性**（≥4.53 會讓輸出變成流暢胡言，#1446/#1953 仍 open）；`onnxruntime-gpu==1.18.0`；`numpy==1.26.4`；`--recursive` 拉 Matcha-TTS；不要在同環境裝 vLLM（會偷升 torch，#1847）（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/main/requirements.txt ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1953 ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1847）。 - **必備護欄（來自大量 issue）**：`prompt_text` 必加前綴 `You are a helpful assistant.<|endofprompt|>`（#1735/#1761）；`fp16=False`、不用 TRT fp16（#1930 NaN）；參考音檔 24 kHz mono 5–15 s、transcript 逐字吻合（#1762）；一句一 call、避免「？」（#1704）；best-of-N≥3 + Whisper CER + 時長/字數比檢查（抓重複與吞尾字 #1902/#1730）+ 去頭尾靜音與 fade（#1786）（https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1703 ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1704 ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1730 ；https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1930）。 - **繁體**：**會念錯**，不是「沒處理」而已——#1764 鈴鐺/蝦/胡蘿蔔 念錯，轉簡體後正常 → `tts_text` 與 `prompt_text` 都必須 OpenCC **t2s**（純字形，不要 tw2sp 換詞）（https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1764 ；https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC）。臺灣讀音（和 hàn、垃圾 lèsè）預期會是大陸讀音，需靠拼音覆寫。 - **多音字語法與 BreezyVoice 不是 1:1**：BreezyVoice 是字後綴 `[:ㄏㄠ3]`；CosyVoice3 是「用聲母 token + 帶調號韻母 token 取代該字」`報道[j][ǐ]予`，token 清單固定於 `CosyVoice3Tokenizer.additional_special_tokens`。需寫 注音→(聲母, 韻母+調號) 轉換表，處理零聲母/ü/iu/ui/輕聲；部分韻母 token 是否齊全 UNVERIFIED（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/tokenizer/tokenizer.py ；https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/example.py）。 - **參考音檔硬限制**：`assert speech.shape[1]/16000 <= 30`（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py）。 - **臺灣腔**：方言表有 Minnan 但那是閩南語非臺灣國語；臺灣腔只能靭參考音檔零樣本帶出，強度 UNVERIFIED。採用門檻：若 2–3 位均一老師音檔的重試率 >~30% 或口音明顯大陸化 → 不切換。 ### 第三候選（僅內部評測，不預設開放）：IndexTTS-2（2.0 checkpoint） - 音色/情感被多數社群評為最強，但：拼音覆寫只在 `pinyin.vocab` 內有效且常被忽略（#625/#669/#686/#792）；短句吞字/多餘靜音 17 個月未修（#187/#58/#617）；2.5 有中文品質回退（#801/#759 無維護者回覆）；2.0 **沒有** duration control（README 明言 not yet enabled）；6 GB VRAM 數字是 2.5 的。License 為 bilibili 自訂：中文版門檻是年收 **1 億**人民幣（英文版寫 10 億，中文版優先）、PRC 法律、輸出算 Derivative Work，且 DISCLAIMER 禁止「未經授權將合成聲音用於商業目的」→ 複製均一老師聲音需取得老師/均一授權。PR #590（繁體自動轉簡）被關閉未合併，作者註明「簡體輸入明顯較好」（https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts ；https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/LICENSE_ZH.txt ；https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/DISCLAIMER ；https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/801 ；https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/625 ；https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/pull/590）。 ### 不採用（附一句理由） - **Qwen3-TTS-1.7B-Base**：Apache、pip 即裝、真 list-batch，但零發音控制（#99/#273 無人回）；#341 參考音檔尾巴會漏到輸出開頭；串流模式語速漂移（#239，需 `non_streaming_mode=True`）；3090 實測 RTF ~3（HF disc #18）；zh-TW 工具回報繁體輸入被念成粵語腔（Augur ADR-005）；repo 自 2026-03-17 停更，issue 由 bot 關閉；且 CER 0.77 並非最低（同表 CosyVoice3 0.71）（https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS ；https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS/issues/341 ；https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astroicers/Augur/main/docs/adr/ADR-005-optional-external-tts.md ；https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice/discussions/18）。 - **GLM-TTS**：RL 權重**未釋出**（README 仍 Coming Soon、#23 維護者確認、#29 open），實際只有 base CER 1.03；flag 是 `--use_phoneme` 非 `--phoneme`，且開啟後韻律卡頓（#35/#36 維護者承認）；fp32 必須；開頭嗶聲 #55 無人回（https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS ；https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/issues/23 ；https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/issues/36 ；https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/issues/55）。 - **VoxCPM2**：Apache、SIM 79.5 最高、內建 denoiser 與 `voxcpm batch`，但無任何發音覆寫 → 多音字無解；可列為 bake-off 第 4 名（https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM）。 - **GPT-SoVITS**：MIT、極活躍（V5 2026-10-05）、G2PW 自動多音字、zh_normalization 內建繁→簡與算式唸法，但安裝最重、無使用者拼音覆寫（PR #1728 未合併）；唯一優勢是同一老師可用 1 分鐘微調，若未來「固定老師」場景出現再評估（https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS ；https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS/pull/1728）。 - **F5-TTS / OmniVoice / Fish / Chatterbox / Spark / MegaTTS3 / MOSS-TTS / Step-Audio-EditX**：分別因 CC-BY-NC 權重、中文品質差（#287）、停更、WaveVAE encoder 未釋出、8B 太重 / torch 2.9.1 stack 等排除（來源見研究報告）。 ### 跨引擎共用的前端（不管哪個引擎都要） 1. 數字/單位/算式 → 繁體中文字（借 GPT-SoVITS `zh_normalization` 的規則順序：RE_ASMD/分數/百分比/小數，`+−×÷=`→加減乘除等）（https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS/main/GPT_SoVITS/text/zh_normalization/text_normlization.py）。 2. `g2pw`（預設繁體、注音輸出）當共用多音字 oracle，lesson.json 可帶每詞讀音；再依引擎輸出 `[:ㄏㄠ3]` 或 `[j][ǐ]`（https://github.com/GitYCC/g2pW）。 3. 非 BreezyVoice 引擎：OpenCC t2s 後才送入；字幕維持繁體。 4. best-of-N by CER：裁判 ASR 必須與 TTS 訓練資料獨立（見第 2 節 A8 偏誤）。 --- ## 2. GPU 前處理流程（prefix.mp4 → 參考音檔 + 文字稿 + 說話者輪廓） ### 環境（三個獨立 venv；階段間以 work/ 內的 WAV/JSON 溝通） ```bash # venv-asr：VAD + ASR + speaker embedding + 輪廓 + CER 裁判（CUDA 12 全靠 pip wheel，不需 root） uv venv ~/.askback/venv-asr --python 3.11 && source ~/.askback/venv-asr/bin/activate pip install "faster-whisper==1.2.1" "ctranslate2==4.8.2" nvidia-cublas-cu12 "nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*" # 4.8.3 才 1 天新，釘 4.8.2 pip install "silero-vad==6.2.3" torch torchaudio "praat-parselmouth==0.4.7" "jiwer==4.0.0" opencc "speechbrain==1.1.1" scikit-learn numpy soundfile export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(python -c 'import os,nvidia.cublas.lib,nvidia.cudnn.lib;print(os.path.dirname(nvidia.cublas.lib.__file__)+":"+os.path.dirname(nvidia.cudnn.lib.__file__))')${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" # 必須在 python 啟動前設定 # venv-sep：音樂分離 + 降噪（48 kHz） uv venv ~/.askback/venv-sep --python 3.11 && source ~/.askback/venv-sep/bin/activate pip install "demucs==4.1.0" deepfilternet # 選配：pip install clearvoice（MossFormer2_SE_48K） # venv-tts：BreezyVoice（py3.10, torch 2.3.1 cu118, d592c9d）不動；venv-tts-cv3：CosyVoice3（py3.10, torch 2.3.1 cu121, transformers 4.51.3） ``` ；https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet ；https://pypi.org/project/speechbrain/ 一次性模型暖機（需網路一次，不需 token）後設 `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`：faster-whisper `large-v3` 與 `SoybeanMilk/faster-whisper-Breeze-ASR-25`、demucs htdemucs、DeepFilterNet3、`speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`。 ### 步驟（嚴格順序；前處理階段一次只駐留一個模型，每階段獨立 process） | # | 步驤 | 工具 / 指令 | VRAM | 備註 | tts.notes:
SCOPE/METHOD: Facts above come from GitHub READMEs, requirements/pyproject files, HF model cards, LICENSE files and GitHub issues fetched 2026-10-14; last-commit dates via api.github.com. Anything marked UNVERIFIED was not confirmed from a primary source. No independent head-to-head Taiwanese-Mandarin benchmark exists for any of these models; the ranking is a judgment weighing (a) license fit for an education product, (b) explicit pronunciation override (needed to port BreezyVoice's bopomofo tagging), (c) published zh CER/SIM, (d) 3090 fit and install friction, (e) maintenance.

KEY FINDINGS vs. the BreezyVoice baseline: (1) Nothing released through Oct 2026 is explicitly trained for 台灣國語 except BreezyVoice itself; MediaTek's 2026 Breeze 3 work ('BreezyVoice 26', BreezyVoice-Taigi arXiv 2603.19259) targets Taiwanese Hokkien and weights are not public (issue #14 unanswered). Every other model inherits the Taiwanese accent only from the reference clip, which LLM-based zero-shot models generally do (OmniVoice and Chatterbox docs explicitly note accent carry-over from the reference), but strength of accent preservation per model is UNVERIFIED and must be measured. (2) Newer models have clearly better similarity/intelligibility than CosyVoice-1-era BreezyVoice on standard benchmarks (Fun-CosyVoice3_RL CER 0.81, Qwen3-TTS WER 0.77, GLM-TTS_RL 0.89, Confucius4 0.94, VoxCPM2 0.97/SIM 79.5 vs CosyVoice2 1.45/75.7); BreezyVoice publishes no CER/SIM. (3) Pronunciation override, essential for 多音字 in teaching content, exists in: IndexTTS-2/2.5 (`<行|HANG2>`), Fun-CosyVoice3 ([j][ǐ] bracketed pinyin), GLM-TTS (--phoneme hybrid), MOSS-TTS / Step-Audio-EditX / OmniVoice (pinyin with tone numbers inline), BreezyVoice (bopomofo [:ㄏㄠ3]); absent in Qwen3-TTS, VoxCPM, Spark-TTS, Chatterbox, Confucius4, Fish; GPT-SoVITS has automatic G2PW only (override PR #1728 unmerged); F5-TTS accepts raw pinyin in gen_text as a hack. A bopomofo→pinyin(tone-number) converter is trivial, so BreezyVoice's G2PW-based auto-tagging can be kept as the front end and re-emitted in each model's syntax.

TRADITIONAL CHINESE: None of the non-BreezyVoice models document zh-TW handling; CosyVoice, GPT-SoVITS and IndexTTS frontends use wetext/WeTextProcessing/zh_normalization + jieba/G2PW built for Simplified, with no OpenCC step (verified in CosyVoice frontend.py and GPT-SoVITS chinese2.py). Qwen/Qwen3-derived tokenizers (CosyVoice2/3, Qwen3-TTS, OmniVoice) contain Traditional characters so synthesis works, but number/unit normalization and polyphone accuracy on Traditional text are UNVERIFIED. Recommended pipeline: OpenCC tw2s (or s2twp inverse) on the script before TTS, keep Traditional only for display subtitles, and apply pinyin overrides after conversion. BreezyVoice already ships opencc-python-reimplemented.

REFERENCE AUDIO FROM TEACHING VIDEOS (noisy/music): No surveyed model documents robustness to music-bearing prompts; research (Interspeech 2024/2025) shows speech-enhancement preprocessing can raise quality metrics but lower speaker similarity. Practical plan: vocal separation (Demucs/UVR-class) → VAD → pick a 5–12 s clean, single-speaker, speech-only segment with ~1 s trailing silence → optional light denoise (VoxCPM has load_denoiser/denoise flag; Step-Audio-EditX has a denoise edit type) → verify with Whisper CER before cloning. Hard limits: CosyVoice/BreezyVoice ≤30 s (assert), F5-TTS ~12 s clip, MegaTTS3 <24 s (moot), Fish 10–30 s minimum-ish. Most LLM-based models need the reference transcript (CosyVoice zero_shot, Qwen3-TTS unless x_vector_only_mode, Spark, GLM (likely), Step-Audio, F5); IndexTTS, VoxCPM 'controllable' mode, Confucius4, OmniVoice (Whisper fallback) and BreezyVoice (Whisper fallback) do not strictly need it. Reuse the sibling project's best-of-N-takes-by-Whisper-CER selection with any of these; for Taiwanese-Mandarin ASR scoring consider MediaTek-Research/Breeze-ASR-26 (HF, found during search; not evaluated here).

3090 FIT: Everything except Fish Drama 3 (≥48 GB) fits; Fish S2-Pro (≥24 GB) is at the limit; MOSS-TTS 8B (~17 GB bf16 weights) is tight but workable; all others ≤~15 GB with most 0.5–2B models at 5–8 GB, leaving room to co-host faster-whisper on GPU. FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere (bf16) for Qwen3-TTS/MOSS. Dependency clash watch: CosyVoice/BreezyVoice pin torch 2.3.1; IndexTTS 2.8; OmniVoice 2.8; MOSS/Step-Audio 2.9.1 + transformers 5.x; Chatterbox 2.6.0 + transformers 5.2 — isolate each in its own venv/uv project.

LICENSES — commercial-safe: Apache-2.0 (CosyVoice/Fun-CosyVoice3, Qwen3-TTS, VoxCPM, GLM-TTS code [weights MIT], MOSS-TTS, Step-Audio-EditX code, Spark-TTS, Confucius4, BreezyVoice, MegaTTS3) and MIT (GPT-SoVITS, Chatterbox). Conditional: IndexTTS (bilibili license; royalty-free under 100M MAU / RMB 1B, PRC law, anti-'improve other AI' clause, revocable). Non-commercial: F5-TTS weights (CC-BY-NC), OmniVoice weights (CC-BY-NC), Fish Speech 1.5 and OpenAudio S1-mini (CC-BY-NC-SA), Fish S2-Pro (Research License), Voxtral TTS (CC-BY-NC, cloning scope in open weights unclear), Higgs Audio v3 (non-commercial per roundup, not surveyed in depth). 

OTHER 2026 RELEASES SEEN BUT NOT FULLY SURVEYED (UNVERIFIED details): Voxtral-4B-TTS-2603 (Mistral, 2026-03-26, CC-BY-NC, cloning possibly API-only), X-Voice (arXiv 2605.05611, 30-language cross-lingual cloning), Higgs Audio v3, VibeVoice (Microsoft, long-form dialogue), MiniMax/Soprano/Muyan/Kimi-Audio (no evidence of open-weight TTS cloning found).

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: build a 3090 bake-off harness in the skill (voices/<name>.wav + .txt → same 10 zh-TW teacher sentences incl. known polyphones and numbers → each candidate in its own venv) scoring Whisper/Breeze-ASR CER, WavLM/ECAPA speaker similarity to the reference, RTF, and a native-speaker blind MOS; shortlist Fun-CosyVoice3_RL, IndexTTS-2(.0), Qwen3-TTS-1.7B-Base, GLM-TTS_RL, VoxCPM2 against BreezyVoice. ## (c) Traditional-Chinese frontend, numbers, polyphones

- BreezyVoice: native 繁體 (trained with bopomofo tags), OpenCC used only to convert Whisper output s2t; bracket tags `字[:ㄏㄠ3]` for manual overrides (README). Its inherited CosyVoice frontend uses WeTextProcessing 1.0.3 `zh_tn_model` for numbers; WeTextProcessing master `Normalizer.__init__` has `traditional_to_simple=True` default (also remove_erhua, full_to_half, remove_interjections, tag_oov; taggers: cardinal, date, fraction, math, measure, money, time, range, sport) — so number verbalization goes through a simplified-oriented FST; whether BreezyVoice's normalizer actually re-simplifies the whole text in v1.0.3 is UNVERIFIED (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenet-e2e/WeTextProcessing/master/tn/chinese/normalizer.py ; https://github.com/wenet-e2e/WeTextProcessing).
- CosyVoice 2/3 (official frontend.py): no opencc/t2s anywhere; Chinese path = wetext `ZhNormalizer(remove_erhua=False)` → punctuation cleanup → token-length split; `<|...|>` in text disables normalization; no g2p in this file (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py). The `wetext` package (pynini-free runtime of WeTextProcessing) defaults `traditional_to_simple=False`, so 繁體 digits/numbers are still verbalized but characters stay Traditional; pinyin inpainting is the polyphone fix (https://github.com/pengzhendong/wetext ; https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512). Whether CosyVoice3 reads 繁體 as well as 簡體 is UNVERIFIED (no issue data retrievable; GitHub search API rate-limited).
- GPT-SoVITS: chinese2.py has no opencc, but its PaddleSpeech-derived `zh_normalization.TextNormalizer.normalize_sentence` runs `tranditional_to_simplified` as step 1, then dates/times/temperature/measure/`RE_ASMD` math (looped)/power/fraction/percent/phone/range/negative int/version/decimal/quantifiers/default numbers, and `_post_replace` maps `+ - × ÷ =` → 加 減 乘 除 等 — so 繁體 input is handled natively and 「1598-260」-style arithmetic is verbalized. G2PW is hardcoded on (`is_g2pw = True`, `G2PWModel`, `style="pinyin"`, `enable_non_tradional_chinese=True`), merged with pypinyin fallback and `polyphonic.rep` dictionaries (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS/main/GPT_SoVITS/text/chinese2.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS/main/GPT_SoVITS/text/zh_normalization/text_normlization.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS/main/GPT_SoVITS/text/g2pw/g2pw.py). Note G2PW in GPT-SoVITS outputs pinyin, so Taiwan-specific readings (e.g. 和 hàn, 垃圾 lè sè) depend on the model's training labels — UNVERIFIED which standard it learned.
- F5-TTS `convert_char_to_pinyin`: rjieba + pypinyin `Style.TONE3, tone_sandhi=True`; no opencc; no number handling at all (digits passed raw) → must pre-normalize numbers and ideally t2s (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SWivid/F5-TTS/main/src/f5_tts/model/utils.py). A discussion confirms traditional chars are simply converted via pypinyin (https://github.com/SWivid/F5-TTS/discussions/883).
- IndexTTS2: Simplified-favoring per PR #590; Kevin Deng's pipeline = OpenCC t2s → jieba → pypinyin (https://skier633.github.io/).
- g2pW (GitYCC, INTERSPEECH 2022, Apache-2.0): default output bopomofo with tone digits (e.g. ㄕㄤ4), `style='pinyin'` optional, `enable_non_tradional_chinese=True` for Simplified input (implying Traditional is the default), trained on CPP; G2PWModel-v2 / -v2-onnx checkpoints; also packaged as pypinyin-g2pW and in PaddleSpeech (https://github.com/GitYCC/g2pW ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GitYCC/g2pW/master/README.md). Leaderboard lists 99.08% CPP accuracy but marked unverified (https://sotaverified.org/tasks/polyphone-disambiguation).
- OpenCC configs for Taiwan: t2s, tw2s, tw2sp (Taiwan→Simplified with Mainland phrases), s2tw, s2twp (Simplified→Taiwan Traditional with Taiwan phrases); Python package `opencc` (https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC).

No zh-TW figure for large-v3-turbo found (UNVERIFIED).

zhtw.recommendations:
1. TTS engine for the AskBack skill (3090, 24 GB): keep BreezyVoice-300M as the primary Taiwanese-Mandarin voice-clone engine — it is still the only open model trained on Taiwanese Mandarin with native 繁體 + bopomofo override, and HEAD is unchanged (d592c9d), so the sibling project's pins (torch 2.3.1 cu118, py3.10) remain valid. Add a pluggable second backend for A/B: Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (Apache-2.0, same CosyVoice lineage, pinyin inpainting, needs ref wav + transcript) — but feed it text that has been number-normalized and, optionally, OpenCC tw2s-converted, and measure Taiwanese-accent retention on a Taiwanese teacher clip before adopting. Avoid Fish/OpenAudio (NC license, no dialect handling) and treat IndexTTS-2.5 as Simplified-favoring (license is bilibili custom).
2. Voice reference contract: voices/<name>.wav (6–15 s clean teacher segment, no BGM — run a vocal separator if the prefix has music) + voices/<name>.txt in 繁體. Cache speaker embeddings (BreezyVoice issues #8/#12) and fix a seed; issue #10 shows CPU results degrade, so always run on GPU.
3. Text frontend (繁體 pipeline): (i) pre-verbalize numbers/arithmetic yourself in 繁體 before any engine (e.g. 「1598-260」→「一千五百九十八減二百六十」; borrow GPT-SoVITS's zh_normalization regex order: RE_ASMD/fraction/percent/decimal, then map +−×÷= → 加減乘除等); (ii) for BreezyVoice pass 繁體 directly and let its g2pW bopomofo tagging run, adding manual `字[:ㄓㄨㄥ4]` tags for known hard polyphones (長/行/樂/重/和/數) from a per-lesson override table; (iii) for CosyVoice3/IndexTTS/F5 variants run OpenCC `tw2s` first and use their pinyin-inpainting syntax for overrides; (iv) run `g2pw` (bopomofo, default Traditional) as a shared polyphone oracle in the agent so the lesson.json can carry per-word readings.

## A. Verified facts per component (as of 2026-10-14)

### A1. VAD
- **silero-vad 6.2.3** (PyPI, released 2026-09-23; Python >=3.8; dep torch>=1.12.0; extras `audio` = torchaudio<2.10 + torchcodec, `onnx-cpu`, `onnx-gpu`). MIT. README states "no telemetry, no keys, no registration"; weights `silero_vad_16k.safetensors` ship inside the package (`src/silero_vad/data`), so it is fully offline after pip install. Supports 8 kHz / 16 kHz only. API: `load_silero_vad()`, `read_audio(path, 16000)`, `get_speech_timestamps(audio, model, threshold=0.5, sampling_rate=16000, min_speech_duration_ms=250, max_speech_duration_s=inf, min_silence_duration_ms=100, speech_pad_ms=30, return_seconds=False, ..., window_size_samples=512)`, `collect_chunks(tss, wav)`. https://pypi.org/project/silero-vad/ , https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/snakers4/silero-vad/master/src/silero_vad/utils_vad.py

- pyannote segmentation and webrtcvad were not chosen: pyannote models are gated (below); webrtcvad is not GPU/ML-grade and was not needed given silero is bundled and MIT.

### A2. Speaker embeddings / dominant-speaker selection (offline, no gated models)
- **3D-Speaker (modelscope)**: Apache-2.0; Python>=3.8, PyTorch>=1.10; models on ModelScope with no token mentioned: `iic/speech_campplus_sv_zh-cn_16k-common` (CAM++, 200k Mandarin speakers, CN-Celeb EER 6.78%), `iic/speech_eres2netv2_sv_zh-cn_16k-common` (EER 6.14% CN-Celeb), `iic/speech_eres2net_sv_zh-cn_16k-common`. Inference: `python speakerlab/bin/infer_sv.py --model_id iic/speech_campplus_sv_zh-cn_16k-common`. Full diarization recipe exists (`speakerlab/bin/infer_diarization.py`; only the *optional* overlap detector needs `--hf_access_token`). Mandarin-trained -> best fit for 均一 teacher voices. https://github.com/modelscope/3D-Speaker (ModelScope model page did not render in fetch; details come from the GitHub README.)
- **SpeechBrain `spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb`**: NOT gated on HF, Apache-2.0, 16 kHz mono, VoxCeleb1-test EER 0.80%; `EncoderClassifier.from_hparams(source="speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb", savedir=...)` then `encode_batch`. speechbrain 1.1.1 on PyPI (2026-08-27, Python>=3.8.1). https://huggingface.co/speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb , https://pypi.org/project/speechbrain/
- **WeSpeaker**: `pip3 install wespeakerruntime` (ONNX, has a CN-Celeb model, `wespeaker.Speaker(lang='chs')`); HF checkpoints `Wespeaker/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM`, `...resnet293-LM` loaded via `wespeaker.load_model_local(dir)`. https://pypi.org/project/wespeakerruntime/ , https://huggingface.co/Wespeaker/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet293-LM
- **pyannote `speaker-diarization-community-1`**: gated (accept conditions + HF token) at *download* time only; after `git lfs clone` it runs fully offline via `Pipeline.from_pretrained('/local/dir')`; CC-BY-4.0; requires pyannote.audio 4.x; `pipeline.to(torch.device("cuda"))`; returns `exclusive_speaker_diarization`. So it is usable, but not "zero-token". https://huggingface.co/pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 , https://github.com/pyannote/pyannote-audio , https://github.com/pyannote/pyannote-audio/discussions/1988
- resemblyzer: not researched further (older GE2E encoder); the three options above cover the need.

### A3. Music / noise removal
- **Demucs 4.1.0** (adefossez/demucs, MIT, Python>=3.10, `python3 -m pip install -U demucs` or `uvx demucs`). Author no longer actively developing it (left Meta for Kyutai) but repo is the maintained fork, not archived. Models: `htdemucs` (default), `htdemucs_ft` (~4x slower, slightly better), `htdemucs_6s`, `mdx_extra`. `--two-stems=vocals` gives vocals + accompaniment at 44.1 kHz stereo int16. VRAM: ~7 GB default, ~3 GB with `--segment 8`; HT models max segment 7.8 s. Known artifacts: phase misalignment, spectral smearing, residual bleed (acknowledged by authors per arXiv 2603.16805). https://github.com/adefossez/demucs , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.16805
- **DeepFilterNet** (`pip install deepfilternet`; MIT/Apache-2.0; torch>=1.9; 48 kHz full-band). Code `DEFAULT_MODEL = "DeepFilterNet3"` in `df/enhance.py` (docstring/CLI help still say DeepFilterNet2 - stale). `init_df()` -> `enhance(model, df_state, audio)`; CLI `deepFilter noisy.wav --output-dir out`; input is loaded at model SR (48 k) and output resampled back to original SR. Models shipped in repo `models/` (DeepFilterNet3.zip etc.). Mask-based (ERB gain + deep filtering) -> non-generative. https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet/main/DeepFilterNet/df/enhance.py
- **ClearerVoice-Studio / clearvoice** (`pip install clearvoice`, Apache-2.0; weights auto-downloaded from HuggingFace, ModelScope fallback, no token mentioned). Models: `MossFormer2_SE_48K`, `FRCRN_SE_16K`, `MossFormerGAN_SE_16K`, `MossFormer2_SR_48K` (super-res), `MossFormer2_SS_16K`, `AV_MossFormer2_TSE_16K`. Own benchmark (VoiceBank+DEMAND 48k): MossFormer2_SE_48K PESQ 3.15 / SI-SDR 19.36 / STOI 0.95 vs DeepFilterNet 3.03 / 15.71 / 0.94 vs Resemble_enhance 2.84 / 12.42 / 0.94 (vendor numbers, not independent). MossFormer2_SE_48K predicts a phase-sensitive mask (non-generative). https://github.com/modelscope/ClearerVoice-Studio , https://github.com/modelscope/ClearerVoice-Studio/blob/main/clearvoice/README.md
- **resemble-enhance** (MIT, 44.1 kHz, `pip install resemble-enhance`, `--denoise_only` flag). Generative pipeline (UNet denoiser + IRMAE + CFM ODE sampler + UnivNet vocoder). Independent URGENT-2025 evaluation: strong non-intrusive scores but "low intrusive scores and CAcc, suggesting a tendency to hallucinate content" -> risky for cloning references. Repo shows little activity (13 commits, 56 open issues). https://github.com/resemble-ai/resemble-enhance , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.02641
- **facebookresearch/denoiser**: archived 2023-10-31, CC-BY-NC 4.0 -> exclude. https://github.com/facebookresearch/denoiser

Treat timbre impact as something to measure in-pipeline (embedding cosine raw vs enhanced).

### A4. Loudness / resampling
- ffmpeg `loudnorm`: two-pass = pass 1 `loudnorm=I=..:TP=..:LRA=..:print_format=json -f null -`, pass 2 with `measured_I/measured_LRA/measured_TP/measured_thresh/offset(target_offset)` and `linear=true`; true peak always guaranteed, LRA not; filter internally upsamples to 192 kHz so you must set `-ar` on output. https://k.ylo.ph/2016/04/04/loudnorm.html , https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html#loudnorm (loudnorm section too deep to fetch; afftdn examples confirmed there)
- Prompt sample rates per TTS (from source code):

G2PW `G2PWConverter` adds inline `[:ㄏㄠ3]` bopomofo for rare chars. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice/main/single_inference.py , https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice
  - CosyVoice (1/2/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512): frontend loads prompt via `load_wav(prompt_wav, 16000)` for speech tokens + speaker embedding and `load_wav(prompt_wav, 24000)` for mel; hard `assert speech.shape[1]/16000 <= 30` ("do not support extract speech token for audio longer than 30s"); warns when synthesis text < 0.5x prompt text length; output `cosyvoice.sample_rate` from config. Fun-CosyVoice3 released 2025/12, Apache-2.0, supports pinyin pronunciation inpainting. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py , https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice

### A5. GPU ASR
- **faster-whisper 1.2.1** (PyPI 2025-10-31, Python>=3.9). GPU needs cuBLAS for CUDA 12 + **cuDNN 9**; "latest ctranslate2 only support CUDA 12 and cuDNN 9"; no-root way: `pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*` + export `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the two wheel `lib` dirs before starting Python; downgrade ctranslate2 to 4.4.0 only for cuDNN 8. - **ctranslate2** PyPI history: 4.8.3 (2026-10-13, one day old), 4.8.2 (2026-08-31), 4.8.1 (2026-07-03), 4.8.0 (2026-06-06), 4.7.2 (2026-05-19). Python 3.9–3.14. https://pypi.org/project/ctranslate2/#history
- **nvidia-cudnn-cu12** latest 9.27.0.42 (2026-09-29); 9.26.1.1 (2026-10-07). https://pypi.org/project/nvidia-cudnn-cu12/
- **Breeze-ASR-25** (MediaTek Research; Whisper-large-v2 fine-tune; Apache-2.0; outputs Traditional Chinese; trained on 10,000 h BreezyVoice-synthesized Mandarin + 1,738 h CommonVoice17-EN + 11 h NTUML2021; paper arXiv 2506.11130). Output script not documented (likely Simplified -> normalize with OpenCC; UNVERIFIED). https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice

### A6. Speaker profile tooling
- **praat-parselmouth 0.4.7** (PyPI 2025-11-27): `pitch = snd.to_pitch(); f = pitch.selected_array['frequency']; f[f==0] = nan` (0 = unvoiced). https://pypi.org/project/praat-parselmouth/ , https://parselmouth.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/plotting.html
- Normative speaking F0 (Leung, Oates, Papp & Chan 2022, J. Voice, Australian English conversation): males ~115 Hz (SD 21), females ~199 Hz (SD 28) per Sydney Voice Lab reference sheet. Other populations differ (Persian males 138 Hz; Black American females 150–168 Hz), so use a dead-band, not a single cutoff. https://www.sydney.edu.au/content/dam/corporate/documents/faculty-of-medicine-and-health/research/research-centres/sydney-voice-lab/acoustic-analysis-normative-data-reference-sheet-20250416_v4.0-sydney-voice-lab.pdf.coredownload.pdf

### A7. Sibling repo check
- Jimmynycu/askback-skill README: BreezyVoice when GPU present, edge-tts fallback; `setup_local_tts.sh` (~8 GB); `tts_local/voices/SOURCES.txt`; Whisper for transcripts in look.py. The README does not expose version strings, prompt-prep, VAD/denoise, or CER details (those live in tts_local/ and pipeline/tts.py per the page). https://github.com/Jimmynycu/askback-skill

### A8. Important bias finding
Breeze-ASR-25's training set is dominated by 10,000 h of audio synthesized by BreezyVoice. Using Breeze-ASR-25 as the *judge* of BreezyVoice takes risks being systematically lenient to BreezyVoice's own pronunciation errors. Use it for the human-teacher prefix transcript (where it is the best zh-TW model), but use an independent ASR (Whisper large-v3 via faster-whisper, optionally SenseVoiceSmall as second opinion) as the CER judge for synthesized takes.

### A9. VRAM reality on a 24 GB 3090
Measured/documented: Demucs ~7 GB default (3 GB with --segment 8); faster-whisper large fp16 ~4.5 GB (int8 ~2.9 GB); VoxCPM2 ~8 GB; BreezyVoice/CosyVoice3 ~2–6 GB (UNVERIFIED, estimate from model size); DeepFilterNet3/CAM++/ECAPA/silero: small (<1 GB, UNVERIFIED). Everything fits simultaneously in theory, but torch + CTranslate2 each keep their own caching allocators and BreezyVoice needs torch 2.3.1/cu118 while ctranslate2 4.8.x needs CUDA 12 + cuDNN 9 pip wheels -> they should live in separate virtualenvs anyway, which forces stage-wise execution.

## B. Recommended stack (all local, Linux, RTX 3090, no API keys)

### B0. Environments (separate venvs; stages talk via WAV/JSON in work/)
```bash
# venv-asr: VAD + ASR + speaker embeddings + profile + CER judge  (CUDA 12 via pip wheels, no root)
uv venv ~/.askback/venv-asr --python 3.11 && source ~/.askback/venv-asr/bin/activate
pip install "faster-whisper==1.2.1" "ctranslate2==4.8.2" "nvidia-cublas-cu12" "nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*"   # 4.8.3 is 1 day old; pin 4.8.2
pip install "silero-vad==6.2.3" torch torchaudio "praat-parselmouth==0.4.7" "jiwer==4.0.0" opencc "speechbrain==1.1.1" scikit-learn numpy soundfile
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(python -c 'import os,nvidia.cublas.lib,nvidia.cudnn.lib;print(os.path.dirname(nvidia.cublas.lib.__file__)+":"+os.path.dirname(nvidia.cudnn.lib.__file__))')${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"   # must be set BEFORE python starts (faster-whisper README)
# optional Mandarin speaker model (3D-Speaker/ModelScope, no token):
pip install modelscope && git clone https://github.com/modelscope/3D-Speaker ~/.askback/3D-Speaker && pip install -r ~/.askback/3D-Speaker/requirements.txt

# venv-sep: music separation + denoise (48 kHz)
uv venv ~/.askback/venv-sep --python 3.11 && source ~/.askback/venv-sep/bin/activate
pip install "demucs==4.1.0" deepfilternet            # optional: pip install clearvoice   (MossFormer2_SE_48K)

# venv-tts: BreezyVoice as today (python 3.10, torch 2.3.1 cu118, commit d592c9d) — unchanged; add Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B / VoxCPM2 as pluggable backends later
```
One-time offline model warm-up (needs network once, never a token): `python -c "from faster_whisper import WhisperModel; WhisperModel('large-v3'); WhisperModel('SoybeanMilk/faster-whisper-Breeze-ASR-25')"`, `demucs -n htdemucs --two-stems=vocals /dev/null || true` (triggers weight download), `python -c "from df import init_df; init_df()"`, `python -c "from speechbrain.inference.speaker import EncoderClassifier as E; E.from_hparams(source='speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb', savedir='~/.askback/models/ecapa')"`. Then set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

### B1. Ordered pipeline: prefix.mp4 -> voices/ref_<case>.wav + .txt + profile.json
**Step 1 — extract audio (keep a 48 k master + a 16 k working copy)**
```bash
ffmpeg -y -i prefix.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le work/a48.wav
ffmpeg -y -i work/a48.wav -ar 16000 -af aresample=resampler=soxr work/a16.wav
```
**Step 2 — music check + vocal isolation (Demucs, GPU, venv-sep)** — run always (prefix is short), but only *use* the stem if music is actually present:
```bash
demucs -n htdemucs --two-stems=vocals --segment 8 -o work/demucs work/a48.wav     # --segment 8 keeps VRAM ~3 GB; drop it for max quality (~7 GB)
# decide: if RMS(no_vocals) is > 30 dB below RMS(mix) -> music absent -> keep a48.wav; else use work/demucs/htdemucs/a48/vocals.wav
```
Rationale: Demucs leaves phase/spectral smearing; never pay that cost when there is no accompaniment. Use `htdemucs_ft` only if residual music is audible after `htdemucs`.
**Step 3 — denoise, conservatively (DeepFilterNet3 default; MossFormer2_SE_48K optional)**
```bash
deepFilter work/vocals_or_a48.wav --output-dir work/dfn      # DEFAULT_MODEL = DeepFilterNet3, 48 kHz in, original SR out
# alternative: python -c "from clearvoice import ClearVoice as C; m=C(task='speech_enhancement',model_names=['MossFormer2_SE_48K']); w=m(input_path='work/vocals_or_a48.wav',online_write=False); m.write(w,output_path='work/mf2.wav')"
```
Gate it: compute speaker-embedding cosine (ECAPA or CAM++) between raw and enhanced; accept the enhanced file only if cosine >= 0.85 (heuristic, tune on a few 均一 videos) AND the raw file's estimated SNR is poor (e.g. silero non-speech RMS within 20 dB of speech RMS). Do NOT use resemble-enhance (generative, hallucination/CAcc concerns in URGENT-2025) or facebookresearch/denoiser (archived, CC-BY-NC) for cloning references.
**Step 4 — VAD (silero-vad 6.2.3, bundled weights, offline)**
```python
from silero_vad import load_silero_vad, read_audio, get_speech_timestamps
m = load_silero_vad(); wav = read_audio('work/clean16.wav', 16000)
ts = get_speech_timestamps(wav, m, threshold=0.5, min_speech_duration_ms=400, min_silence_duration_ms=300, speech_pad_ms=100, max_speech_duration_s=12, return_seconds=True)
```
**Step 5 — dominant-speaker selection (no gated models)**: cut each VAD segment into 1.5 s windows -> embeddings with `speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb` (16 kHz) or, preferably for Mandarin, 3D-Speaker CAM++ `iic/speech_campplus_sv_zh-cn_16k-common` -> `sklearn.cluster.AgglomerativeClustering(metric='cosine', linkage='average', distance_threshold=0.45)` (threshold heuristic) -> cluster with the most total speech time = teacher. If the top cluster < 60 % of speech (two cartoon characters alternating), keep both clusters' profiles and let the agent pick the one that is the explainer/narrator; expose this in profile.json. Optional upgrade: pyannote `speaker-diarization-community-1` cloned once with an HF token, then run from local dir with `pipeline.to(torch.device('cuda'))`; use its `exclusive_speaker_diarization` when 2 characters overlap. Skip speaker selection entirely if silero finds speech but clustering yields 1 cluster (typical 電子黑板 single teacher).
**Step 6 — pick & assemble the reference clip**: among the teacher's segments choose 3–10 s segments with (a) no other-speaker windows, (b) lowest residual accompaniment energy (vocals/no_vocals ratio per segment), (c) no clipping; concatenate with 200 ms silence to 8–15 s total. Hard limit **< 30 s** (CosyVoice frontend asserts <= 30 s on the 16 kHz prompt). Two-pass loudnorm on the master and emit both rates:
```bash
ffmpeg -i work/ref_master.wav -af loudnorm=I=-18:TP=-2:LRA=7:print_format=json -f null - 2> work/ln.json   # read input_i, input_tp, input_lra, input_thresh, target_offset
ffmpeg -y -i work/ref_master.wav -af "loudnorm=I=-18:TP=-2:LRA=7:measured_I=..:measured_LRA=..:measured_TP=..:measured_thresh=..:offset=..:linear=true" -ar 48000 work/ref48.wav   # loudnorm upsamples to 192 kHz internally; -ar is mandatory
ffmpeg -y -i work/ref48.wav -ac 1 -ar 16000 -af aresample=resampler=soxr voices/ref_<case>.wav       # BreezyVoice/CosyVoice tokens+spk-emb, VoxCPM2 input
ffmpeg -y -i work/ref48.wav -ac 1 -ar 24000 -af aresample=resampler=soxr voices/ref_<case>_24k.wav   # CosyVoice 24 kHz mel path, avoids 16k->24k upsample
```
(-18 LUFS / -2 dBTP is a speech-prompt heuristic, not a vendor spec.)
**Step 7 — transcripts (faster-whisper, venv-asr)**: Breeze-ASR-25 (CT2 fp16) for the human teacher: best zh-TW numbers (CV16-zh-TW 7.97 vs 8.95; ML-lecture 4.98 vs 6.41) and native 繁體 output, no OpenCC needed.
```python
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
asr = WhisperModel('SoybeanMilk/faster-whisper-Breeze-ASR-25', device='cuda', compute_type='float16')   # ~4.5 GB class
segs,_ = asr.transcribe('voices/ref_<case>.wav', language='zh', beam_size=5, vad_filter=False, condition_on_previous_text=False)
ref_txt = ''.join(s.text for s in segs).strip()   # -> voices/ref_<case>.txt ; also run on full prefix -> work/transcript.json (replaces look.py CPU whisper)
```
Write `voices/ref_<case>.txt` only after a human-free sanity check: CER between Breeze and large-v3 outputs on the same clip < 0.15; otherwise flag the reference as low-confidence (bad transcripts silently wreck zero-shot cloning).
**Step 8 — speaker profile (profile.json, used to pick nearest consented bank voice)**
```python
import parselmouth, numpy as np, json
snd = parselmouth.Sound('voices/ref_<case>.wav'); p = snd.to_pitch(pitch_floor=60.0, pitch_ceiling=500.0)
f = p.selected_array['frequency']; f = f[f>0]
f0_med = float(np.median(f)); f0_mean=float(np.mean(f)); rng_st = 12*np.log2(np.percentile(f,95)/np.percentile(f,5))
gender = 'male' if f0_med < 155 else 'female' if f0_med > 185 else 'uncertain'      # dead band; Leung 2022: M~115+-21 Hz, F~199+-28 Hz
cjk = [c for c in ref_txt if '一'<=c<='鿿']; rate = len(cjk)/speech_seconds_from_vad       # chars/sec on speech-only time
emb = ecapa_or_campplus_embedding('voices/ref_<case>.wav').tolist()
json.dump(dict(gender=gender,f0_mean=f0_mean,f0_median=f0_med,f0_range_semitones=rng_st,chars_per_sec=rate,embedding=emb,speaker_share=share,music_present=music,enhanced=used_dfn), open('voices/ref_<case>.profile.json','w'))
```
Nearest bank voice = argmin over bank of `(1-cos(emb, bank_emb)) + 0.3*|log2(f0_med/bank_f0)| + 0.1*|rate-bank_rate|` (weights heuristic). Each bank entry: `voices/<name>.wav` (16 k mono, <=15 s, loudnormed), `voices/<name>.txt`, `voices/<name>.profile.json` produced by the same Step 8.
**Step 9 — pronunciation check loop (synthesize -> ASR -> CER -> retake)**: N=3 takes per beat (vary seed) -> judge with an ASR *independent of the TTS training data*: faster-whisper `large-v3` float16 (co-resident, ~4.5 GB) with `language='zh'`, `initial_prompt='以下是繁體中文的教學內容。'`; normalize hyp and ref with `opencc.OpenCC('s2twp.json')`, strip punctuation/whitespace, map Arabic digits to 中文數字 both sides; `jiwer.cer(ref, hyp)`; accept min-CER take if CER <= 0.08, else regenerate with G2PW/bopomofo inline hints on the offending characters (`[:ㄏㄠ3]`) up to 2 more rounds; fall back to best take and log. Optionally add SenseVoiceSmall as a second judge and take the max CER (conservative). Keep Breeze-ASR-25 out of the judge role (trained on 10k h of BreezyVoice audio -> leniency bias).

### B2. VRAM budget & scheduling on the 3090
- Preprocessing (Steps 2–8) is strictly sequential, one model resident at a time (Demucs 3–7 GB -> DFN3 <1 GB -> ECAPA/CAM++ <1 GB -> Breeze/large-v3 ~4.5 GB fp16). Each stage is a separate process so the allocator is freed (`del model; torch.cuda.empty_cache()` is not enough across torch + CTranslate2).
- Synthesis loop (Step 9): co-host TTS (BreezyVoice ~2–6 GB est.; VoxCPM2 ~8 GB) + Whisper large-v3 fp16 ~4.5 GB in two processes -> < 15 GB of 24 GB, leaving headroom for CUDA context + batched ASR (batch 8 adds ~1.5 GB). Use `compute_type='int8_float16'` (~3 GB) if a heavier TTS backend (VoxCPM2 / IndexTTS-2.5) is enabled.
- Never co-host Demucs with TTS; it is a one-shot preprocessing step.

### B3. TTS backend note (secondary to this task)
No October-2026 model was found that is *verified* for Taiwanese-Mandarin accent + bopomofo control like BreezyVoice. Keep BreezyVoice as default and make the backend pluggable behind the same (ref16k.wav, ref.txt) interface; candidates worth an A/B on CER + speaker cosine + a Taiwanese listener: Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (Apache-2.0, pinyin inpainting, same 16 k prompt path, <30 s), VoxCPM2 (Apache-2.0, 16 k in / 48 k out, prompt_text, ~8 GB), Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base (Apache-2.0, ref_text, no phoneme control). IndexTTS-2.5 has a restrictive bilibili license.

facts.corrections:
VERDICT: Most substantive claims (license, 30 s prompt, CER 0.81, pinyin inpainting, Minnan, torch pin, python 3.10, no Traditional handling, slow cadence) are CONFIRMED against primary sources, but two decision-relevant claims are wrong (the model identifier and the "1:1 mapping" from BreezyVoice tags) and one is unverifiable (VRAM). Details:

1. MODEL ID IS WRONG. "FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512_RL" does not exist as a Hugging Face or ModelScope repo. HF API https://huggingface.co/api/models/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512_RL returns no model (id null); ModelScope API https://www.modelscope.cn/api/v1/models/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512_RL returns "record not found"; the HF page https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512_RL returns 401. "_RL" is only a row label in the benchmark table (README line 81, https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/blob/main/README.md). The RL weights ship as the file `llm.rl.pt` inside the single repo https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (file list: llm.pt, llm.rl.pt, flow.pt, hift.pt, speech_tokenizer_v3.onnx, CosyVoice-BlankEN/..., cosyvoice3.yaml). Correct identifier: FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (HF, created 2025-12-11, lastModified 2026-02-03, gated=false, 185k downloads) with llm.rl.pt swapped in for llm.pt. How exactly the loader selects llm.rl.pt (rename vs. config) is UNVERIFIED — README grep shows no instructions.

2. LICENSE — CONFIRMED, no correction. Repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0 verbatim (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/LICENSE), HF cardData license: apache-2.0 (https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512/raw/main/README.md). No non-commercial restriction; the RL weights are in the same Apache-2.0 repo.

3. "PINYIN INPAINTING MAPS 1:1 FROM BREEZYVOICE'S BOPOMOFO TAGS" — WRONG / OVERSTATED. BreezyVoice uses a SUFFIX annotation after the character with bopomofo + tone digit: `今天天氣真好[:ㄏㄠ3]` (https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice). CosyVoice3 REPLACES the character with separate initial and final-with-diacritic special tokens: `高管也通过电话、短信、微信等方式对报道[j][ǐ]予好评。` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/example.py). The bracket tokens are a fixed inventory of additional_special_tokens in CosyVoice3Tokenizer (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/tokenizer/tokenizer.py, lines ~274-310): initials [b]..[zh],[j],[q],[x],[y],[w] and finals with tone marks ([ǐ],[iǎn],[uǎng],[ǘ],[ǚ],[ǜ],[vè],...) plus toneless forms ([a],[ian],[iu],...). Migration therefore needs a bopomofo→(initial, final+diacritic) conversion table, tone-digit→diacritic conversion, zero-initial/ü/iu/ui spelling rules, and a change from suffix-annotation to character-substitution. Deterministic, but not 1:1 and not drop-in. Also the inventory looks incomplete for some finals (e.g. no bracketed [üe]/[üan] forms beyond [vè]) — UNVERIFIED how those are meant to be written.

4. MINNAN — CONFIRMED but not useful for this project. "Minnan" appears in the 18+ dialect list on the README and model card; there is NO Minnan instruct example in example.py (only Cantonese: 'You are a helpful assistant. 请用广东话表达。<|endofprompt|>'), and Taiwanese Mandarin / Traditional Chinese / 台灣 are never mentioned anywhere (README, model card, example.py). Minnan (Hokkien) is a different language from Taiwanese Mandarin and is irrelevant to Junyi lecture voices.

5. ≤30 s PROMPT — CONFIRMED: cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py line 97: `assert speech.shape[1] / 16000 <= 30, 'do not support extract speech token for audio longer than 30s'` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py). Zero-shot cloning API: `inference_zero_shot(tts_text, prompt_text, prompt_wav, zero_shot_spk_id='', stream=False, speed=1.0, text_frontend=True)`; also `add_zero_shot_spk(prompt_text, prompt_wav, id)` to cache a speaker (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/cosyvoice/cli/cosyvoice.py).

6. zh CER 0.81 — CONFIRMED: README table row "Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512_RL | 0.5B | test-zh CER 1.21→0.81 | SS 77.4 | test-en WER 1.68 | test-hard CER 5.44" (https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice#readme, https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512). Note RL slightly lowers speaker similarity (78.0→77.4 zh, 71.8→69.5 en), which matters for voice cloning.

7. TORCH/PYTHON PINS — CONFIRMED with one correction: requirements.txt pins torch==2.3.1, torchaudio==2.3.1, transformers==4.51.3, onnxruntime-gpu==1.18.0, numpy==1.26.4, with `--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice/main/requirements.txt). So the pin is cu121, NOT cu118 like the current BreezyVoice env — a separate venv is needed; it cannot share BreezyVoice's torch 2.3.1 cu118 install. Python: README says `conda create -n cosyvoice -y python=3.10`. vLLM optional path: vllm 0.9.0 + transformers 4.51.3 or vllm 0.11.0 + transformers 4.57.1.

8. NO TRADITIONAL HANDLING — CONFIRMED: frontend.text_normalize uses ttsfrd or wetext ZhNormalizer only; grep for opencc/tradition/zh-tw/hant in frontend.py, cosyvoice.py, model.py, frontend_utils.py returns nothing. Model card language list is plain "zh". OpenCC t2s before synthesis must stay in our pipeline. Whether the Qwen2.5-0.5B-based LLM was trained on any Traditional text is UNVERIFIED.

9. "SAME LINEAGE / MIGRATION CARRIES OVER" — PARTIALLY WRONG. BreezyVoice is derived from CosyVoice v1 (300M, own tokenizer, speech_tokenizer v1); CosyVoice3 is a different stack (Qwen2.5-0.5B-style text tokenizer in CosyVoice-BlankEN/, speech_tokenizer_v3, DiT flow, CosyVoice3Tokenizer). Pipeline-side pieces that are model-agnostic DO carry over (G2PW polyphone disambiguation, OpenCC, best-of-N with Whisper CER), but the annotation format, model classes and env do not. BreezyVoice also ships batch_inference.py (CSV-driven); CosyVoice3 has no batch API — inference_zero_shot is a per-text generator; throughput options are vLLM (`load_vllm=True`) and NVIDIA Triton TRT-LLM runtime (README 2025/08).

10. VRAM — UNVERIFIED. No official VRAM figure in README or model card. fp32 weights total ~3.4 GB (llm.pt 2.02 GB, flow.pt 1.33 GB, hift.pt 83 MB per https://nexgpu.net/en/models/cosyvoice/); secondary sources range from ~4 GB (https://ai-engineering-trend.medium.com/alibaba-open-sources-cosyvoice-3-a-new-benchmark-in-0-5b-parameter-speech-synthesis-7ddbb8e9ec22) to 8 GB+ (https://comfy.icu/extension/filliptm__ComfyUI_FL-CosyVoice3) to 12 GB+ recommended with vLLM (nexgpu). Any of these fits a 24 GB RTX 3090; `fp16=True` is supported (cosyvoice.py) but the README warns the DiT TensorRT fp16 engine "have some performance issue".

11. RECENCY / "SLOW REPO CADENCE" — CONFIRMED. field.corrections:
VERDICT (practitioner view): Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (+ llm.rl.pt) is a *conditionally* acceptable choice for an unattended zh-TW pipeline synthesizing ~10 short sentences per video — but ONLY because the existing BreezyVoice pipeline already has best-of-N takes gated by Whisper CER. As a bare single-shot generator it is NOT reliable: real-world reports (Dec 2025–Oct 2026) show frequent hallucination, sentence repetition, prompt-text leakage, dropped trailing characters, and large run-to-run variance. Nearly all of these are catchable by a CER gate + retry, which is why I do not mark the claim refuted. Several claims in the model description need correction (below).

=== 1. Hallucination / repetition / instability — REAL and widely reported ===
- #1703 "Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B的效果简直就是噩梦" (Dec 18 2025, ~20 commenters, auto-closed by stale bot May 2026, zero maintainer replies): repeated sentences ("动不动就把某些句子重复一遍"), "完全没有CosyVoice2-0.5B稳定", reference transcript spoken at start, prompt text leaking into output, long unnatural pauses, pinyin hotfix tags not working for one user. Community fixes: (a) prompt_text MUST be prefixed "You are a helpful assistant.<|endofprompt|>" (v3-only requirement, not needed in v2), (b) fp16=False to avoid long silences, (c) 24 kHz reference audio to avoid crackle, (d) prompt_text must match prompt audio word-for-word. But one user explicitly says the prefix "不是万能的" — repetition still occurred; the OP tested identical seeds on v2 and v3 and reverted to CosyVoice2. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1703
- #1735 (Dec 25 2025) "大概率出现胡言乱语" in zero-shot; root cause = missing <|endofprompt|> prefix. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1735
- #1761 English partial repetition only in v3, fixed by the prefix. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1761
- #1702 "零样本克隆效果不如cosyvoice2，很大概率会有杂音或者胡说一小段"; maintainer asked if prefix was missing; no follow-up. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1702
- #1902 (May 31 2026): with prefix present, a sentence in a ~95-char passage is randomly read twice; user's "fix" was appending "！！！"; no maintainer reply, stale-closed. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1902
- #1704 (Dec 2025): second sentence of multi-sentence zero-shot randomly balloons (16.8 s vs 6.68 s), "doesn't exist on CosyVoice2"; a "?" in text made the next sentence overlong. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1704
- #1730 (Dec 24 2025): inference_zero_shot drops last 1–2 characters in ~10% of outputs; no confirmed fix. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1730
- #1733: prompt text synthesized into output even WITH the prefix present for the OP. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1733
- #1770: same text + params → durations 28–39 s for a 33 s clip, large pitch/rate variance (sampling is stochastic; no seed guidance). https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1770
- #1915 (Jul 2026): good cloning but "occasional unexplained pauses"; commenter: "说话说的好慢啊，中间停顿时间较长". https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1915
- #1825: mixed zh/en text → garbled or dropped content (relevant for math/English terms in lessons). https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1825
- Paper itself: "generating rare words, tongue twisters, and domain-specific terms remains difficult"; repeated words are hard cases for the reward model; DiffRO-EMO "can adversely affect pronunciation". https://arxiv.org/html/2505.17589v2
- Independent LoRA repo (RTX 3090 Ti, Aug 2026): long-form zero-shot Base WER 0.281 (PyTorch) / 0.505–0.774 in other runs; ASR found "corrupted, repeated, and reference-derived content"; CosyVoice3 "sensitive to <|endofprompt|> placement". https://github.com/instavar/cosyvoice3-lora-finetuning
=> Mitigation for unattended use: fixed prompt template with prefix; one sentence per call (short, no "?" if possible); best-of-N (N≥3) with Whisper CER gate + duration sanity check (reject if duration/char ratio outside band, catches repetition/truncation); trim leading/trailing silence.

=== 2. Audio artifacts NOT catchable by CER (residual risk) ===
- #1688 "普遍电音比较大… 无法达到生产级别"; maintainer: use latest code, check TensorRT version, compare to Space. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1688
- #1762 v3 "电音" where v2 stable; maintainer: use 24 kHz prompt ("cv3建议用24k音频作为prompt"); artifact not resolved; maintainer notes v3 timbre is closer than v2. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1762
- #1786 noise/pops at start/end, "more common in zero-shot"; stale-closed. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1786 ; cosyvoice.cpp #33 adds fade-in to hide start transients; owner notes first seconds can have abnormal pitch/timbre. https://github.com/Lourdle/cosyvoice.cpp/issues/33
- #1797 >2 s leading silence (prefix-related). https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1797
- #1930: load_trt=True + fp16=True → NaN audio 64/64 on official checkpoint; use fp16=False (TRT fp32 works). Code itself warns "DiT tensorRT fp16 engine have some performance issue". https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1930
=> Keep fp16=False, feed 24 kHz mono WAV reference 5–15 s (fengin deploy repo: 16 kHz mono, 5–15 s; HF discussion #10: 24 kHz mono, bypass Gradio numpy path), apply fade-in/out + silence trim, and add a cheap artifact check (e.g., clipping/NaN/RMS, optional DNSMOS) alongside CER.

=== 3. Traditional Chinese: WORSE than "no handling" — actively mispronounces 繁體 ===
- #1764 (Jan 2026, Traditional-text user): locally 鈴鐺/蝦/胡蘿蔔/渾 pronounced wrong vs ModelScope demo; resolved by converting tts_text to Simplified ("转成简体后…效果一样"). https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1764
=> OpenCC t2s (tw2s) on tts_text is MANDATORY, and the prompt transcript too. Note tw2s also changes vocabulary (e.g., 軟體→软件) which the Taiwanese teacher voice will then say in PRC wording — use OpenCC "t2s" (character-only) not "tw2sp" to keep Taiwan vocabulary; UNVERIFIED whether the model pronounces Taiwan-specific words (垃圾 lèsè, 和 hàn, 企業 qì) in Taiwan or PRC readings — no user reports found; expect PRC readings and fix via pinyin inpainting.

=== 4. Taiwanese-speaker voice cloning: NO real user reports found ===
- Searched GitHub, HF, V2EX, Zhihu, CSDN, Taiwanese blogs: zero first-hand reports of cloning a Taiwanese Mandarin speaker with CosyVoice3. Only a Taiwanese blog (2026-06-07) asserts "它的聲音比較接近台灣腔" with no listening test and inconsistent facts (lists CosyVoice 3 as 1.5B, CER 0.71%). UNVERIFIED. https://blog.markkulab.net/post/ai-voice-clone-lora-training-guide
- Dialect list: "Minnan" is in the README (Guangdong, Minnan, Sichuan, Dongbei, Shan3xi, Shan1xi, Shanghai, Tianjin, Shandong, Ningxia, Gansu…) but Taiwan Mandarin / 台灣腔 is NOT named anywhere in README or paper. https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2505.17589v2
- #1792 "粤语 zero-shot 效果很差" shows dialect zero-shot is weak in practice. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1792
- BreezyVoice paper's explicit motivation was that CosyVoice sounds PRC-accented for Taiwanese use. https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17790v1
=> Accent carry-over from a Taiwanese reference is plausible (zero-shot cloning copies prosody/accent partially) but unproven; must A/B listen before adoption.

=== 5. Pinyin inpainting / "maps 1:1 from bopomofo" — PARTIALLY WRONG ===
- Format is split initial+final with tone DIACRITIC: 報道[j][ǐ]予 (verified README line 179, example.py line 94). BreezyVoice uses [:ㄏㄠ3] (tone digit, whole syllable). Conversion bopomofo→(initial, final-with-diacritic) is deterministic but needs a small table (zero-initial syllables, ü, erhua, neutral tone) — not literally 1:1. https://github.com/mtkresearch/BreezyVoice
- Paper reports 100% correction on only 15 zh + 9 en cases (tiny set). https://arxiv.org/html/2505.17589v2 ; one #1703 commenter reported hotfix tags not working; an M3 Max blog verified [j][ǐ] works. https://zhchxiao123.github.io/posts/cosyvoice3-deployment-guide/
- No G2PW/polyphone frontend in CosyVoice3 ("without a traditional frontend module") — so BreezyVoice's G2PW tagging step must be kept on your side and emitted as pinyin tags.

=== 6. "Same lineage as BreezyVoice so migration carries over" — OVERSTATED ===
BreezyVoice derives from CosyVoice v1 (300M, arXiv 2407.05407); CosyVoice3 is a Qwen2-based LLM with a new tokenizer (speech_tokenizer_v3), new prompt convention (<|endofprompt|>), different API (AutoModel/CosyVoice3 class). What carries over: reference wav+transcript workflow, OpenCC, Whisper best-of-N CER gating, G2PW→pinyin tag emission. What doesn't: code, env, bopomofo syntax.

=== 7. RL weights — load path needs a hack ===
- llm.rl.pt (2.02 GB) ships in the same HF repo as llm.pt (file list verified; repo lastModified 2026-02-03, 185k downloads). https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512/tree/main
- cosyvoice/cli/cosyvoice.py CosyVoice3.__init__ hard-codes `self.model.load('{}/llm.pt'…)`; there is no flag to pick llm.rl.pt — you must rename/symlink llm.rl.pt→llm.pt (maintainer in #1780: "use the llm.rl.pt in … model repo"). https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1780
- RL trades SIM for CER: test-zh CER 0.81 vs 1.21 but SIM 77.4 vs 78.0; test-hard 5.44/75.0 (model card). Note the "0.81 CER" is on SEED test-zh (Simplified, PRC speakers) — no zh-TW number exists.

=== 8. Install on Linux + CUDA 12 + RTX 3090 — workable but brittle ===
- requirements.txt pins torch==2.3.1 / torchaudio==2.3.1 via --extra-index-url cu121 (NOT cu118), onnxruntime-gpu==1.18.0 (needs Microsoft onnxruntime-cuda-12 feed), transformers==4.51.3, numpy==1.26.4, tensorrt-cu12==10.13.3.9, Python 3.10. 3090 (sm_86) is supported by torch 2.3.1+cu121. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/main/requirements.txt
- HARD requirement: transformers must stay 4.51.3. ≥4.53 (incl. 4.57.x, 5.x) makes v2/v3 output collapse into fluent gibberish (0% character recall) due to a frozen attention mask in Qwen2Encoder.forward_one_step; still OPEN Oct 2026, no upstream fix. #1953 https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1953 ; #1446 (24 comments, since Jul 2025) https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1446 ; #1706 (downgrade from 4.57.3 to 4.51.3 fixed example.py output; another user still had prompt-content leakage) https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1706 ; #1886 https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1886 ; #1777 https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1777
- Installing vLLM silently upgrades torch (0.9.0→torch 2.7) and breaks the eager path; users call the version matrix "乱成一锅汤"; one working combo reported torch 2.8.0 + vllm 0.11.0; instavar verified torch 2.9.1+cu128 / transformers 4.57.6 / vllm 0.15.1 (contradicts the 4.51.3 rule — only in vLLM path). #1847 https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1847
- Other pitfalls: --recursive submodule (Matcha-TTS), libcudnn.so.8 (pin nvidia-cudnn-cu12==8.9.7.29 in non-vLLM mode), numpy<2, openai-whisper build needs setuptools<80 (#1844), ttsfrd optional (cp310 linux wheel, falls back to wetext). https://github.com/fengin/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512-Deploy ; https://liudon.com/posts/voice-cloning-solution-comparison/
- VRAM on RTX 3090: ~5.2 GB (fengin, measured on 3090); 5–6 GB peak (V2EX user). Fits easily alongside faster-whisper.
=> Recommendation: isolated conda/uv env, pin exactly to requirements.txt, do NOT install vLLM in the same env, do a smoke test that runs example.py and ASR-verifies the output (catches the transformers trap automatically).

=== 9. Inference time per sentence ===
- No published plain-3090 benchmark. Closest: RTX 3090 Ti, mean generation 5.04 s (PyTorch eager) vs 2.75 s (vLLM) per ~7 s clip; vLLM RTF 0.178. https://github.com/instavar/cosyvoice3-lora-finetuning
- RTX 4070 laptop: RTF 0.8–1.6 (V2EX OP, Dec 2025); CPU-only RTF ≈10. https://v2ex.com/t/1179310
- RTX 4090 on Windows/WDDM with wrong env: eager fp16 RTF 2.4–3.3 (kernel-launch bound), CUDA-graph 0.76–0.95 — illustrates env sensitivity. https://github.com/QwenAudio/CosyVoice/issues/1927
- M3 Max MPS: ~1.8–2.3× realtime (21 s for 10.7 s audio). https://zhchxiao123.github.io/posts/cosyvoice3-deployment-guide/
- First call cold ~6 s, ~2–3 s after warmup (fengin).
=> On a 3090, eager fp32 single-sentence (5–8 s audio) ≈ 4–8 s; 10 sentences × best-of-3 ≈ 2–4 min wall-clock plus Whisper scoring — acceptable for an offline video pipeline. Use stream=False, speed=1.0, keep one model instance resident.

=== 10. Repo cadence / support — CONFIRMED slow ===
GitHub moved FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice → QwenAudio/CosyVoice (301). Last main commit 2026-05-25 (README links); last functional commits Feb–Mar 2026. Most 2026 issues get only an "aluminumbox" auto-answer bot reply and are stale-closed after 44 days ("Fun-CosyVoice 3.5" announced elsewhere but not open-sourced; #1840). Expect no upstream fixes; vendor your patches (transformers mask fix from #1446/#1953 comments if you want newer transformers).

=== 11. Reddit / YouTube ===
No Reddit threads reachable (reddit.com blocked to this crawler; web search surfaced none). No YouTube comparisons found. UNVERIFIED gap; community feedback lives in GitHub issues, V2EX, Zhihu, CSDN.

=== Bottom line for the skill ===
Keep CosyVoice3-2512 (RL weights) as the primary candidate, but gate adoption on a one-time A/B with 2–3 Junyi teacher references vs BreezyVoice: measure Whisper CER, retry rate, and listen for accent/artifacts. Mandatory guardrails: exact prefix template, transformers==4.51.3/torch 2.3.1 cu121 env, OpenCC t2s on both texts, 24 kHz mono 5–15 s reference whose transcript matches exactly, fp16=False, no TRT fp16, one sentence per call, best-of-N≥3 with CER + duration-ratio + clipping checks, silence trim + fade. If retry rate on real teacher voices exceeds ~30% or accent is clearly PRC, fall back to BreezyVoice (same guardrails).

facts.corrections:
Verified against primary sources on 2026-10-14. The claim is mostly right on pins, pinyin control and activity, but several decision-relevant points are wrong or unverifiable for the exact checkpoint the claim recommends (2.0):

1. "duration control" (for the 2.0 checkpoint) — WRONG. The GitHub README's own IndexTTS-2 release note says: "precise synthesis duration control ... *This functionality is not yet enabled in this release.*" (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts README, line ~43). Only IndexTTS-2.5 exposes a speaking-speed knob, `duration_factor` (0.5–2.0, applied in indextts/infer_v2_5.py as `target_lengths = int(S_infer.shape[1]*1.72*duration_factor)`), which is a global speed multiplier, not a target-duration control. So if we pick 2.0, we get emotion control but NO duration control; if we pick 2.5 we get a speed factor only.

2. "6 GB VRAM" — ONLY stated for 2.5, UNVERIFIED for 2.0. The "roughly 6 GB of VRAM for inference, Python 3.10–3.11" line is on the IndexTTS-2.5 model card (https://huggingface.co/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5, README line 47). The IndexTTS-2 card (https://huggingface.co/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2) and the GitHub README give no VRAM figure for 2.0; community numbers for 2.0 range 6–12 GB (e.g. https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/585, RTX 3060 12 GB run). Irrelevant for a 3090 (24 GB) but the number should not be attributed to 2.0.

3. License — partly WRONG / incomplete. (a) Thresholds: the English LICENSE §2.2 says >100M MAU or annual revenue >RMB 1 billion requires a separate license (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/LICENSE), but the Chinese LICENSE_ZH.txt §2.2 says 年收入超过1亿人民币 (RMB 100 million) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/LICENSE_ZH.txt), and §9 of the English text says the Chinese version prevails on any conflict. This 10x discrepancy was raised in https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/228 (2026-08-15 comment) with no maintainer answer. (b) The repo DISCLAIMER (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/DISCLAIMER) additionally prohibits "f) 未经授权将合成声音用于商业目的" (using synthesized voices commercially without authorization) and "a) 合成...未经授权的个人声音" — i.e. cloning the Junyi teacher's voice needs the teacher's/Junyi's authorization, and the README says "For commercial usage and cooperation, please contact indexspeech@bilibili.com". (c) Correct parts: governing law is PRC (§6.1, Shanghai Arbitration Commission §6.2); §3.4(c) is the anti-distillation clause ("may not Use ... to improve any AI model, except ... non-commercial AI models"); "Derivative Work" explicitly includes model outputs (§1.5). The same license text (naming "bilibili indextts2") ships on both HF repos (IndexTTS-2: LICENSE.txt + LICENSE_ZH.txt; IndexTTS-2.5: LICENSE). Net: for an educational, non-revenue use on a 3090 the license is workable, but "commercial OK under thresholds" overstates it — the controlling Chinese threshold is RMB 100M revenue, and the DISCLAIMER adds a voice-authorization requirement.

4. Traditional Chinese / Taiwanese Mandarin — UNVERIFIED as claimed, with negative signals: pyproject.toml classifier is "Natural Language :: Chinese (Simplified)"; PR #590 "feat: Add OpenCC dependency and auto-convert Traditional Chinese" (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/pull/590) states "the model performs significantly better with Simplified Chinese input" and was CLOSED UNMERGED on 2026-03-13; no opencc/t2s code exists in indextts/utils/front.py or webui.py on main. Neither the GitHub README nor either HF card mentions 繁體/zh-TW. Practical consequence: we must run OpenCC t2s on lesson.json text before inference, and polyphones (e.g. 行/得/地) need the pinyin override. Taiwanese-accent cloning quality is untested anywhere I could find.

5. Pinyin control — CORRECT. 2.5: `<字|PINYIN2>` form, e.g. `他在银<行|XING2>里<行|HANG2>走了半天。` (HF 2.5 README line ~100; GitHub README "IndexTTS2.5 — Pinyin / CMU phonemes / Japanese Kana"). 2.0: mixed char+pinyin, e.g. `之前你做DE5很好...也DEI3做DE2很好才XING2` (GitHub README ~line 380), valid syllables in checkpoints/pinyin.vocab.

6. Python/torch pins — CORRECT. pyproject.toml on main: `requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.12"`, `torch==2.8.*`, `torchaudio==2.8.*`, `transformers==4.52.1`; `.python-version` = 3.11.13 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/pyproject.toml). Note pyproject `version = "2.0.0"` while README ships both infer_v2.py (2.0) and infer_v2_5.py (2.5) from the same tree.

7. Zero-shot from a short reference — CORRECT in spirit, unstated length. README/model cards say "clones a voice from a single reference audio clip" with no min/max length; code truncates the speaker prompt to 15 s (`_load_and_cut_audio(spk_audio_prompt, 15)` in indextts/infer_v2.py line ~454; emotion prompt also 15 s @16 kHz). So longer teacher clips are silently cut to the first 15 s — pick the reference window deliberately.

8. Batch API — NONE (claim did not assert one, but noting for the decision). `IndexTTS2.infer()` is single-request; `setup_caches(max_batch_size=1)` and `autoregressive_batch_size = 1` in infer_v2.py / infer_v2_5.py; no batch method. Production/concurrent serving for 2.5 only via vLLM-Omni (`vllm serve IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5 --omni --trust-remote-code`, vLLM >=0.27.0, recipe updated 2026-08-12, https://recipes.vllm.ai/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5). Best-of-N takes therefore mean N sequential calls (~0.8B model, fine on a 3090).

9. Recency — CORRECT. Latest commit 2026-09-29 ("fix: 末尾加淡出..." #806), ~24.5k stars (GitHub API). IndexTTS-2.5 released 2026/08/10 (README news; HF repo created 2026-08-10, lastModified 2026-08-12); IndexTTS-2 released 2025/09/08 (HF lastModified 2026-01-20). Tech report arXiv 2601.03888 (Jan 2026).

10. "2.5 Chinese-quality regression report" — CORRECT and still unresolved. #801 "[2.5 中文质量回归] 与 2.0 的可复现盲测..." opened 2026-08-29, open, 0 comments, no maintainer reply (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/801); #759 "为什么感觉情感色彩上没有2.0好" open since 2026-08-12 with 7 user +1 comments, no maintainer reply; #781 closed 2026-08-18 without comments. All are user reports (single-listener A/B), not official benchmarks; the official CV3-Eval table shows 2.5 zh WER 4.36 / SS 77.10 (README Table 1), no 2.0 comparison published.

11. Minor: 2.5 model size ~0.8B (HF 2.5 card); 2.0 size not stated on its card. 2.5 languages: zh, en, ja, es, ar (no Traditional variant). 2.5 text-emotion control requires `use_qwen_emo=True` (QwenEmotion sub-model, in checkpoints).

Decision impact: the claim's headline for 2.0 ("emotion + duration control, 6 GB") is wrong on duration and unsourced on VRAM; license needs the 1亿 threshold and the DISCLAIMER voice-authorization clause; Traditional input needs a mandatory OpenCC pre-step that upstream rejected adding.

A third-party comparison also concedes 2.5's "极致音色相似度略逊于2代" (https://www.yuntts.com/1039.html). So: stay on 2.0 for Chinese cloning.

2. "best explicit pronunciation override" — REFUTED / overstated. The override is only honored when the syllable exists in checkpoints/pinyin.vocab (BPE vocabulary), and multiple reports show overrides silently ignored even for common syllables: 得<dei3> still read "de" (#625, open since 2026-01-05; https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/625); 藏 zang4 → zang1 depending on context, 掊 pou3 unsupported because "POU3" is not in the BPE vocab, closed "completed" without fix (#669 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/669, #674 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/674); shao3 → shao4, maintainer only said "下一版本，会有所缓解" then closed (#686 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/686); on 2.5 the new tag syntax <要|yao4> still produced yao1, closed without fix, only user workaround was to strip to bare "yao4" (#792 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/792). The 2.0 README itself says "拼音控制并非对所有声母韵母组合都生效" (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/blob/main/docs/README_zh.md). Practical consequence: an agent cannot assume an override will take; it must check the pinyin against pinyin.vocab and verify with ASR. The sibling project's G2PW-bopomofo approach (BreezyVoice) remains a more deterministic polyphone path for zh-TW.

3. Hallucination / dropped words / instability on short text — REAL, recurring and unresolved for 17+ months: #187 "会吞词" (open since 2025-05-29; after the first comma everything lost, intermittent, varies by reference clip and GPU; maintainer only asked for repro audio; contributor workaround = fix seed and re-roll; https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/187); #404 (v2: trailing character dropped, 秒 read as English "S"; https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/404); #617 吞字, user workaround is wrapping text in "..." (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/617); #58 short (<10 char) sentences produce 10–30 s of silence/stretched pauses, runaway token 52, was "fixed" then REOPENED and still open (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/58); #207 some voices repeat phrases (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/207); #210 sentence-final punctuation ignored, sentences merged (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/210); #678 秒 → "S" again in Apr 2026, open (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/678); #822 stray "chi" phoneme inserted during cloning, Sep 2026, open (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/822). Model-card limitation: long text is split into segments joined by silences, prosody does not carry across boundaries (https://huggingface.co/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5). The askback use case (~10 short Mandarin sentences, often short lesson phrases with numbers/units like 秒/公分) hits exactly the failure modes above (short text, trailing numerals, units). Unattended use REQUIRES an ASR-CER gate with retries.

4. Taiwanese-speaker / Traditional Chinese quality — UNVERIFIED, no real reports found. GitHub issue search for 繁体/繁體/台湾/台灣/traditional returns nothing relevant; docs/README_zh.md explicitly lists "Simplified Chinese" as the supported language; Linux text normalization is WeTextProcessing (mainland-oriented) per pyproject (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/pyproject.toml). The only Taiwan-specific artifact is a community web tool that feeds Common Voice Taiwan Mandarin clips as reference voices and claims "台灣口音" output, with no evaluation (https://github.com/achir1015/indextts2-taiwan-tts). The Dcard thread (https://www.dcard.tw/f/talk/p/259977173) could not be fetched (403); search snippet only says accent/speed/pauses "may need improvement". Reddit is blocked to this crawler, so Reddit evidence is UNVERIFIED. Recommendation if used: OpenCC t2s before the frontend, and inject pinyin for Taiwan readings (e.g. 和 han4, 垃圾 le4se4, 法 fa4, 液 yi4) — but see item 2: overrides are not guaranteed.

5. "6 GB VRAM" — that figure is the 2.5 model card (https://huggingface.co/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5), not 2.0. Third-party 2.0 measurements: ~7.8 GB FP16 (https://www.cnblogs.com/sensorsen/p/21367537), 14 GB on a 4090 Laptop with author recommending ≥16 GB (https://github.com/mirfahimanwar/TTS-Model-Comparison-Chart/). A 3090 (24 GB) is fine either way.

6. "torch 2.8 / py3.10–3.11" — CONFIRMED: pyproject pins requires-python >=3.10,<3.12, torch==2.8.*, torchaudio==2.8.*, transformers==4.52.1, cu128 index (explicit), deepspeed==0.17.1 optional, flash-attn optional, WeTextProcessing Linux-only (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/index-tts/index-tts/main/pyproject.toml); README says CUDA Toolkit 12.8+ (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts). No 3090-specific issues found (sm_86 is covered by cu128 wheels; the only compute-capability complaint is Pascal sm_60, #815). Linux pain points reported: `uv sync --all-extras` fails at DeepSpeed build (#304), CPU-only torch pulled in if torch not pre-installed from cu128 index (CSDN guides), HF LFS budget exceeded / HF_ENDPOINT leftovers / w2v-bert, campplus, BigVGAN, MaskGCT codec downloads needing manual fetch (https://liudon.com/posts/voice-cloning-solution-comparison/), `CUDA device-side assert` after ~200 sequential syntheses on Ubuntu + torch 2.8 with VRAM growing 8→25 GB, open, no maintainer reply (#364 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/364), stream-capture/illegal-memory errors with the accel/DeepSpeed engine under concurrency (#677). For ~10 sentences per video these are tolerable; recommend a fresh process per video and skipping DeepSpeed/accel extras.

7. Inference time — official 2.0 fp16 RTF 0.33 on RTX 4090 with kv_cache (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts); Faster-IndexTTS-2 paper measured the stock PyTorch FP32 model at 4.19 s latency / RTF 0.76 for Chinese on an A100 and notes PyTorch FP16 is >20% SLOWER than FP32 on that setup (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.21042); 4090 Laptop RTF ~0.8 (comparison chart); RTX 3060: RTF 13 → 1.6 only after `--fp16 --cuda_kernel --gui_seg_tokens 80` (#585 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/585); RTX 5090 on a 2.8 s clip RTF 1.16 because fixed per-call overhead dominates short sentences (#584 https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/issues/584). No 3090 benchmark exists; extrapolating (3090 ≈ 0.5–0.7× a 4090) gives RTF ≈ 0.5–1.0 → roughly 3–6 s per 5-s sentence, i.e. ~1–2 min for 10 sentences, ×N for best-of-N. UNVERIFIED estimate. Note bf16 is slower than fp32 on pre-Ampere cards (#785); on the 3090 use fp16/bf16 but benchmark both.

8. License — CONFIRMED and slightly worse than stated: bilibili Model Use License: separate license needed if >100M MAU or >RMB 1B annual revenue; §3.4(c) "may not Use ... to improve any AI model" (except non-commercial); PRC law, Shanghai Arbitration Commission; Chinese text prevails; "Derivative Work" is defined to include model OUTPUTS (https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/blob/main/LICENSE). Several Chinese blogs wrongly say Apache 2.0 — ignore them. For a Junyi Academy educational use the thresholds are not a problem; the PRC-law/outputs-as-derivative clause is a policy question for the project owner.

9. "active" — commits yes (last 2026-09-29, perf/webui fixes; https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts/commits/main), but quality/pronunciation issues get essentially no maintainer engagement; 17 of the 25 newest issues are open and several were closed as "completed" with no fix (#669, #674, #781, #792).

NET RECOMMENDATION FOR ASKBACK: keep BreezyVoice (or another TW-tuned model) as the default zh-TW voice; treat IndexTTS-2 (2.0, fp16, no DeepSpeed) as an optional high-fidelity backend only behind a mandatory faster-whisper CER gate (reject >~5% CER, retry with new seed, cap N), OpenCC t2s + pinyin injection validated against pinyin.vocab, sentence-level synthesis with "..." padding and trailing-unit checks. Do not adopt 2.5 while #801/#759/#800 are unanswered.

3. "3 s clone": the only primary-source statement is the marketing line "Base model capable of 3-second rapid voice clone from user audio input"; neither README nor HF card states any min/max reference duration or a quality benchmark at 3 s.
