VERDICT: The claim as written ("Apache-2.0, pip-install, batch API, lowest zh WER 0.77, 3 s clone, streaming; only downsides = no pronunciation control, #341, quiet repo") is OVERSTATED. Real-world reports show Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base zero-shot cloning is NOT reliable for unattended zh-TW use out of the box; it is only workable behind a substantial guard stack, and it is effectively unmaintained. Treat it as a conditional candidate, not a default.

FACT CHECK OF THE CLAIM
- Apache-2.0, `pip install -U qwen-tts` (Python 3.12 recommended), list-batch API (`generate_voice_clone` takes lists of text/language; `create_voice_clone_prompt` caches the reference), streaming, "3-second" clone: CONFIRMED on the GitHub README and HF card.
- "lowest zh WER 0.77": WRONG. 0.77 is the 1.7B-Base Seed-TTS test-zh number, but the README's own table shows CosyVoice 3 at 0.71 zh, so it is not the lowest. The release date is 2026-01-22 (arXiv 2601.15621).
- "zero pronunciation control": CONFIRMED. No pinyin/phoneme/SSML input documented on README or HF card; Discussion #53 (stress/pronunciation control, opened 2026-01-24, poll 16 votes) has no maintainer reply as of 2026-10-08. Two zh-TW tools (toufuim/audio-repair-lab; astroicers/Augur ADR-005) work around this by converting text 繁→簡 with OpenCC before inference "降低部分中文字形造成的錯音".
- "#341 tail-echo": CONFIRMED but mischaracterised: it is a LEADING echo — the first ~1.0–1.9 s of output replays the end of the reference transcript before the requested text (Spanish reporter, 2026-07-09; 2nd user 2026-08-20: happens ~half the time for one of six voices). Raising repetition_penalty and greedy decoding do not fix it. Workarounds: remove the reference's final phrase; pad 0.5 s silence to the reference (ocdevel guide, community advice); transcribe the head of the output with word timestamps and trim anything matching the tail of ref_text. No maintainer response; bot-labelled inactive 2026-10-04.
- "repo quiet since Mar 2026": CONFIRMED and worse than "quiet": last commit 2026-03-17 ("fix finetuning bug"); issues #89, #239, #290, #318, #343 were all closed "not planned" by the GitHub bot with zero maintainer replies; PRs #351 and #362 are unreviewed. There is no open-weights successor: Qwen-Audio-3.0-TTS (2026-07-20) is API-only (UNVERIFIED beyond a third-party blog + the X thread lacking a weights link).

REAL-WORLD FAILURE MODES RELEVANT TO UNATTENDED zh-TW
1. Taiwanese accent / Traditional input: Augur ADR-005 (RTX 4070, qwen-tts 0.1.1, Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base, 2026-10-06) reports "繁體輸入被使用者聽成廣東話腔、簡體輸入才是國語" and "描述裡原本寫「台灣口音的國語」，模型念成廣東話"; accepted cost "口音是標準普通話，不是台灣腔". NOTE this is via the VoiceDesign path; for ICL cloning the accent comes from the reference (ocdevel: accent is not controllable; clone from 10–15 s of real accented audio). audio-repair-lab (zh-TW tool, Base clone) says "這不保證台灣口音或每個聲調都正確，仍須試聽". NO published report of cloning a Taiwanese speaker specifically was found; whether a 3 s clone of a 均一 teacher preserves 台灣腔 and tones is UNVERIFIED.
2. Polyphone (多音字) errors: NO concrete reports found either way (only an anecdotal CSDN post claiming VoiceDesign handles 多音字 well). UNVERIFIED; but with no pinyin input there is no fix other than homophone rewriting.
3. Hallucination / runaway (no EOS): ocdevel calls EOS loops "the most common issue"; LocalAI docs say runaway happens more often on SHORT inputs; #318: deterministic hang (27/30 cases) on mixed-script text, never returns; dev.to German test of 1.7B: 3/40 raw sentences "derailed" into ~20 s of unrelated fluent speech with no error, 6/12 mispronunciations vs Polly 3/12; a text-normalisation layer removed derailments on held-out sentences. Augur had to calibrate a hard cap (~0.21–0.25 s/char, max_new_tokens from char count, 502 on overflow) because the model would "念兩三遍都擋不住".
4. Short-sentence instability: #343 (fine-tuned 1.7B, LoRA) ~15% of short/opening utterances have wrong timbre or gender flip; ocdevel: ICL mode "sometimes has a rough start on the first word"; HF CustomVoice discussion #18: sentence-split chunks "sound noticeably different from each other" even with identical settings; ocdevel: zero-shot timbre varies run to run. For a 10-sentence pipeline this means per-sentence timbre drift unless one cached clone prompt is reused and a list-batch call is made.
5. Speaking-rate drift: #239 / #290 — in default streaming mode cloned speech speeds up over >~100 chars and pauses are compressed; PR #362 (unmerged) measured +16.7% drift with a 12.9 s reference, 0.0% with non_streaming_mode=True. The pipeline MUST pass non_streaming_mode=True and keep the reference ≤ ~5–10 s.
6. Install/perf on Linux + CUDA 12 + 3090: pip install works; FA2 is optional (missing FA2 is a warning, falls back to eager). HF discussion #18: RTX 3090 24 GB, CUDA 12.x, torch 2.5, bf16: RTF ~3x (1 min audio in 3 min), GPU util 10–12%, ~8 GB VRAM. HF disc #5: attn_implementation="flash_attention_2" reportedly has no effect (cu130 build; UNVERIFIED for cu12x). Augur (RTX 4070): 1.56–2.05 s per 1 s of audio, 4.6 GB VRAM bf16, cold first utterance 31.5 s (needs warm-up), vLLM-Omni hung on first request. #89: community forks (dffdeeq/Qwen3-TTS-streaming, andimarafioti/faster-qwen3-tts) with torch.compile + CUDA graphs get RTF <0.5, with clicking artefacts reported. Secondary blog claim of RTF 0.95 on a 3090 is UNVERIFIED. Practical estimate for ~10 sentences (~50 s audio) on a 3090 with stock qwen-tts: ~1.5–3 min per take; best-of-3 ≈ 5–8 min, acceptable for an unattended 30–90 s video but not fast.

MINIMUM GUARD STACK IF ADOPTED (all derived from the reports above): OpenCC 繁→簡 on both ref_text and target text; non_streaming_mode=True; reference 5–10 s, trailing 0.5 s silence, strip the final phrase of ref_text; cache one clone prompt and synthesise all sentences in one list call; max_new_tokens derived from character count (~0.25 s/char ≈ 3 frames/char at 12.5 Hz) with a wall-clock timeout; Whisper (faster-whisper zh) CER best-of-N with rejection of outputs whose head matches the tail of ref_text; text normalisation of digits/English letters; homophone rewrite for known 多音字. This is essentially the same best-of-N/CER scaffolding the sibling project already needed for BreezyVoice, so Qwen3-TTS does not remove that complexity.

CONFIDENCE NOTES: Most evidence is GitHub issues, HF discussions and blog tests in English/Spanish/German/Thai; no systematic Taiwanese-Mandarin clone evaluation exists publicly; Reddit was not accessible to the crawler.

Either way: no commercial-use or non-commercial restriction anywhere; both licenses are permissive. Correct statement: code Apache-2.0, weights tagged MIT on HF, commercial use allowed.

3. "Undocumented torch / python" — WRONG. requirements.txt pins torch==2.3.1, torchaudio==2.3.1, torchvision==0.18.1, transformers==4.57.3, onnxruntime_gpu==1.19.0, WeTextProcessing==1.0.3, gradio==6.1.0, deepspeed==0.14.5 — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/main/requirements.txt. README line 43: "Ensure you use Python 3.10 - Python 3.12 versions." Note torch 2.3.1 is the same pin BreezyVoice uses, so no advantage there; Blackwell users report kernel-image problems with that torch (issue #9 thread — https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/issues/9), not relevant to a 3090 (Ampere).

4. "Undocumented params" — not in README, but derivable: HF llm/config.json is LlamaForCausalLM, hidden 2048, 28 layers, vocab 98304, torch_dtype float32; model.safetensors.index.json total_size = 6,208,036,864 bytes → ~1.55B params in fp32 (6.2 GB on disk for the LLM alone) — https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-TTS/resolve/main/llm/config.json and .../llm/model.safetensors.index.json. The paper reportedly lists 1.5B (UNVERIFIED — arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14291 does not state it; the figure came from a search snippet of the PDF).

5. VRAM — correctly "undocumented" officially (no VRAM in README or HF card). Secondary evidence: inference loads the LLM in torch.float32 by default (glmtts_inference.py per issue #9) and a user ran it on a 16 GB RTX 5060 Ti — https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS/issues/9. The vLLM-Omni recipe (updated 2026-06-15) reports ~18–20 GB total (AR ~10 GB + DiT ~8 GB, peak ~16.6 GiB) on 1x A40 and says it fits 24 GB cards — https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-TTS. Fits a 3090 (24 GB) with the plain PyTorch path; headroom is modest if Whisper CER-reranking runs on the same GPU. UNVERIFIED on a 3090 specifically.

6. Phoneme flag — the actual argparse flag is `--use_phoneme` (glmtts_inference.py line 456, and glmtts_inference.sh `args="" # "--use_phoneme" or ""`). The README's `--phoneme` (lines 123, 207) is a documentation error; `--phoneme` will fail. Hybrid phoneme+text "Phoneme-in" for polyphones (example 行 xíng/háng) is real and G2P is pypinyin + custom lexicon (utils/glm_g2p.py) — https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-TTS. Benchmarks were run WITHOUT phoneme mode (README line 207).

7. jsonl batch CLI — VERIFIED. `python glmtts_inference.py --data=<name>` loads examples/<name>.jsonl via jsonl_generate() (lines 333–340); rows are {"uttid","prompt_text","prompt_speech","syn_text"} (examples/example_zh.jsonl). No Python API is documented; the batch path is file-driven.

8. 3–10 s zero-shot prompt — VERIFIED (README Features; HF card "with just 3-10 seconds of prompt audio"). Streaming — VERIFIED as a listed feature (flow.py streaming; vLLM recipe streams by default).

9. Traditional Chinese / Taiwanese Mandarin — NOT claimed by the project anywhere (README, README_zh, HF card, arXiv abstract mention only Chinese + English; no 繁體/Traditional/Taiwan hits in repo or issues). Mechanically: when ttsfrd is not installed (the default pip path), the frontend falls back to WeTextProcessing ZhNormalizer (cosyvoice/cli/frontend.py lines 45, 143–148) constructed WITHOUT overriding traditional_to_simple, whose default is True in WeTextProcessing 1.0.3 (verified from the wheel: `traditional_to_simple=True` in Normalizer.__init__). So 繁體 input is silently converted to 簡體 before G2P/tokenization — it will run, but readings follow Mainland pypinyin conventions, not Taiwan readings (e.g. 和/垃圾/法), and no bopomofo-aware polyphone tagging like BreezyVoice's G2PW. Taiwanese Mandarin accent would come only from the reference prompt audio; whether training data covers it is UNVERIFIED (paper says 100k h, languages not broken down — https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14291).

10. Recency — open-sourced 2025-12-11, paper 2025-12-16/17 (arXiv v1 only), last repo commit 2026-04-10, HF weights last modified 2026-01-12, zero releases/tags, RL weights and "2D Vocos vocoder update" both still "Coming Soon" after 10 months. Project appears maintenance-mode.

Net for our decision: GLM-TTS base is a legitimate Apache/MIT, 1.5B, torch 2.3.1 zero-shot cloner that fits a 3090, with a working jsonl batch path and phoneme override — but it does NOT deliver CER 0.89 today, and it has no Taiwanese-Mandarin-specific front end, so its advantage over BreezyVoice for 均一 videos is unproven and must be measured empirically.

field.corrections:
VERDICT: Not a safe default for an unattended zh-TW pipeline today. The entry as written is inaccurate in two load-bearing ways, and the real-world reports that exist are mixed-to-negative. It can still be a *candidate* behind a best-of-N + Whisper-CER gate, but it does not beat BreezyVoice on the zh-TW axis on any evidence I could find.

1. "GLM-TTS_RL ... CER 0.89" — the RL checkpoint is NOT downloadable (verified 2026-10-14). HF tree of zai-org/GLM-TTS contains only flow/, hift/, llm/, speech_tokenizer/, vocos2d/, vq32k-phoneme-tokenizer/ (HF API tree). README (EN and ZH) still lists "[Coming Soon] Model Weights Optimized via Reinforcement Learning". Maintainer on issue #23 (2025-12-15): "base版本，rl版本还在路上:)". HF's own request (issue #29, 2025-12-17) has zero replies. So the only runnable model is the base (paper CER 1.03 on seed-tts-eval zh, self-reported). Fix the entry to "GLM-TTS (base), RL weights unreleased".

2. License: HF model card says MIT (confirmed via HF API tag license:mit). Correct.

3. Taiwanese-speaker cloning: ZERO user reports found (searched EN/ZH-CN/ZH-TW, GitHub, HF discussions, Reddit: no Reddit threads exist at all). Only data point is the tech report Table 1: the *speech tokenizer's ASR* CER on a "Taiwan Mandarin" set is 16.92 (vs 49.09 for GLM4-Voice) — that is tokenizer-level, not TTS output, and 16.9% is high. Training data: 100k h zh+en, mainland sources; no zh-TW breakdown. Code check (cloned repo): inference text frontend is jieba + pypinyin + WeTextProcessing zh normalizer; there is NO Traditional→Simplified conversion on the inference path (zhconv is imported only in grpo/ reward code). configs/G2P_replace_dict.jsonl ships with 2 entries, simplified-keyed. Behaviour on 繁體 input with Taiwanese readings (e.g. 垃圾/和/法/期) is UNVERIFIED; expect jieba segmentation and pypinyin polyphone defaults to follow PRC readings.

4. Mispronunciation / swallowed words / pauses: official issue #15 (opened 2025-12-11, still open): with the OFFICIAL example sentence, cloning produced random pauses, 轻拂→"宽行", 庞 and 希望 swallowed. Maintainer reply: check that prompt audio and prompt text match ("一般这种问题都是prompt本身音频和文本没有对应"); another user (tool2d) said it read fine for him and was "比隔壁的indextts2好很多". Issue #45 (closed): the frontend appends a space to normalized prompt_text, which caused "偶发的多字" (occasional extra words) when use_cache=false. Issue #55 (2026-07-23, open, no maintainer reply): "每次开头都会滴滴滴然后再说话" — beep at the start of every synthesis. Issue #26: inserted non-existent English was caused by ttsfrd; maintainer says do not use ttsfrd (not a model bug).

5. Polyphone (--phoneme) mode has a prosody cost: issues #35/#36 (2025-12-19): after enabling the polyphone dictionary, synthesis "变得卡顿了不少，尤其是在多音字位置"; maintainer admitted "这一版由于训练时候多音字比例设置的问题，可能会在一些case上影响韵律". The paper's PER improvement (13.23%→5.14%) is on an internal hard-case set; the official eval was run WITHOUT the phoneme flag. So the "fix for polyphones" trades correctness for choppiness — bad for unattended use.

6. Short sentences / hallucination: no GLM-TTS-specific report of short-sentence hallucination found. One hands-on blog (sonusahani.com, 2025-12-11, RTX 6000 48GB) reports cloned output consistently truncated to ~2 s regardless of text length (cause UNVERIFIED). A LINUX DO user (2025-12-22, RTX 3060Ti 8GB) ranked it last: "GLM-tts也太拉了，声音不像还捧读！！很人机，好呆。而且很慢" (IndexTTS2 > CosyVoice3 > GPT-SoVITS > GLM-TTS). An audio.cpp issue reporter (2026-10-02) wrote "reviews on GLM-TTS are pretty bad" (secondhand; that issue itself was a GGUF CRLF bug, not the model). A Zhihu tier report reportedly puts it in the bottom tier "T3" — page returned 403, UNVERIFIED (search snippet only). Positive hands-on: a CSDN RTX 3090 writeup calls short-sentence output natural but notes misrecognized prompt text yields stiff delivery.

7. Precision: inference loads the 1.5B LLM in torch.float32 (glmtts_inference.py line ~430); maintainer on issue #5: "if the open-source ckpt directly uses bfloat16 for inference, some pronunciations will be unclear". So fp32 is effectively mandatory; a user on a 5060Ti reports only 40% GPU utilization.

8. VRAM on a 3090: fine. Measured reports: 8.6 GB peak at 24 kHz with KV cache, 9.7 GB at 32 kHz (CSDN RTX 3080 10GB test, torch 2.9.0+cu118); "需要9G显存, 至少12G" (issue #17); "<10 GB" (sonusahani); 8–10 GB in batch on an RTX 3090 (CSDN). vLLM-Omni path uses ~18–20 GB on an A40 ("fits 24 GB cards").

9. Inference time per sentence: A100-40GB: ~27 ms/token AR, LLM 4.0 s + flow 0.6 s per typical sentence, RTF 0.75; maintainer: "A100 speed is basically as expected" (issue #51). 5060Ti: RTF 1.64 (issue #3). 4090D: slower than real time, no reply (issue #43). RTX 3090: "<8 s" for a 6-s prompt + short sentence; batch of 100 clips took ~25 min (~15 s/clip) (CSDN). Expect roughly 5–15 s per sentence on the 3090, i.e. 1–3 min for 10 sentences, more with best-of-N. Acceptable for offline use; TTFA is poor for interactive use.

10. Linux/CUDA 12/3090 install: feasible but not clean. requirements.txt pins torch==2.3.1, torchaudio==2.3.1, onnxruntime_gpu==1.19.0, numpy==1.26.4, transformers==4.57.3, WeTextProcessing==1.0.3 (needs pynini), deepspeed==0.14.5, openai_whisper. Python 3.10–3.12. Issue #3: pip ResolutionImpossible on py3.10/3.11; maintainer fixed an onnxruntime-gpu CUDA-11 lookup bug; users succeeded by dropping version pins + torch cu128. Issue #42: pynini fails via pip (use conda-forge pynini=2.1.5). Issue #37 tn.chinese, #50 ttsfrd assertion (pip uninstall ttsfrd), #17 gradio 6 hangs at "Loading HiFT" (use gradio 5). None are 3090-specific; Ampere is fine. Note the torch 2.3.1 pin is the same one BreezyVoice uses, so the two cannot trivially share an env with newer torch.

11. Maintenance risk: last commit 2026-04-10 (Ascend NPU support); HF repo last modified 2026-01-12; 46 open issues; multiple issues since Jan 2026 unanswered (incl. #55 beep). Streaming in the open code is simulated (AR finishes before flow chunks; issue #13).

12. What is good: seedable (seed_util.set_seed, default 0) + RAS/nucleus sampling (top_p 0.8, top_k 25), so best-of-N with Whisper CER gating works; jsonl batch CLI exists (examples/*.jsonl); MIT; 3–10 s prompt; VRAM easily fits a 3090 alongside faster-whisper.

Practical recommendation for the AskBack skill: keep BreezyVoice as the zh-TW default; treat GLM-TTS (base) as an optional engine only if the agent validates each take with Whisper CER and rejects takes with leading beeps/truncation. Do not enable --phoneme by default (prosody regression). Nothing in the public record shows GLM-TTS has been validated on Taiwanese Mandarin.
field.confidence: medium — the RL-weights and VRAM/speed facts are verified from the repo, HF API and maintainer replies; quality judgments rest on a handful of hands-on reports (GitHub issues, one LINUX DO post, two CSDN posts, one EN blog) with none from Taiwanese speakers, and no Reddit/YouTube/HF-discussion evidence exists at all.
